title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays. The overall run time complexity should be O(log (m+n)).

title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
description: You are given an integer array target. You have an integer array initial of the same size as target with all zeros. In one operation you can choose any subarray from initial and increment each value by one. Return the minimum number of operations to form a target array from initial.

title: N-Queens
description: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Given an integer n, return all distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle. You may return the answer in any order. Each solution contains a distinct board configuration of the n-queens' placement, where 'Q' and '.' both indicate a queen and an empty space, respectively.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, split nums into k non-empty subarrays such that the largest sum of any subarray is minimized. Return the minimized largest sum of the split.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: Given an array of integers heights representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.

title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
description: There are n people standing in a queue, and they are numbered from 0 to n - 1 in order. You are given an array heights of distinct integers where heights[i] represents the height of the ith person. A person can see another person to their right in the queue if everybody in between is shorter than both of them. Return an array ans of length n where ans[i] is the number of people the ith person can see to their right in the queue.
constraints: All values in heights are unique.

title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
description: Given the head of a linked list, reverse the nodes of the list k at a time, and return the modified list. k is a positive integer and is less than or equal to the length of the linked list. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of k then left-out nodes, in the end, should remain as it is. You may not alter the values in the list's nodes, only nodes themselves may be changed.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is n.

title: Sudoku Solver
description: Write a program to solve a Sudoku puzzle by filling the empty cells. A sudoku solution must satisfy all of the following rules: Each of the digits 1-9 must occur exactly once in each row, column, and 3x3 sub-box. The '.' character indicates empty cells.
constraints: It is guaranteed that the input board has only one solution.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: You are given an array of k linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted linked-list and return it.
constraints: lists[i] is sorted in ascending order.
The sum of lists[i].length will not exceed 10^4.

title: Maximal Rectangle
description: Given a rows x cols binary matrix filled with 0's and 1's, find the largest rectangle containing only 1's and return its area.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: The median is the middle value in an ordered integer list. Implement the MedianFinder class to support adding numbers from a data stream and finding the current median.
constraints: There will be at least one element in the data structure before calling findMedian.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to addNum and findMedian.

title: Text Justification
description: Given an array of strings words and a width maxWidth, format the text such that each line has exactly maxWidth characters and is fully (left and right) justified.
constraints: words[i] consists of only English letters and symbols.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. Return the max sliding window.

title: Candy
description: There are n children standing in a line. Each child is assigned a rating value given in the integer array ratings. Each child must have at least one candy, and children with a higher rating get more candies than their neighbors. Return the minimum number of candies you need to distribute.

title: Basic Calculator
description: Given a string s representing a valid expression, implement a basic calculator to evaluate it, and return the result of the evaluation.
constraints: Every number and running calculation will fit in a signed 32-bit integer.

title: First Missing Positive
description: Given an unsorted integer array nums. Return the smallest positive integer that is not present in nums. You must implement an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Viewers Turned Streamers
description: Write a solution to find the number of streaming sessions conducted by each user whose first activity on the platform was as a viewer. Return the result table ordered by the number of streaming sessions in descending order, then by user_id in descending order.
constraints: session_type is an ENUM of type ('viewer', 'streamer').

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes in the sequence has an edge connecting them. Given the root of a binary tree, return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 3 * 10^4].

title: Count Number of Trapezoids II
description: Given a 2D integer array points where points[i] = [xi, yi] represents the coordinates of the ith point on a 2D plane, return the number of unique non-degenerate trapezoids that can be formed using any four distinct points from points.

title: Russian Doll Envelopes
description: You are given a 2D array of integers envelopes where envelopes[i] = [wi, hi] represents the width and the height of an envelope. One envelope can fit into another if and only if both the width and height of one envelope are greater than the other. Return the maximum number of envelopes you can Russian doll.

title: Guess the Word
description: You are given an array of unique strings words where words[i] is six letters long. One word was chosen as a secret word. Implement an algorithm that uses Master.guess(word) to discover the secret word within the allowed number of guesses.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All words in words are unique.

title: Reverse Pairs
description: Given an integer array nums, return the number of reverse pairs in the array. A reverse pair is a pair (i, j) where 0 <= i < j < nums.length and nums[i] > 2 * nums[j].

title: Wildcard Matching
description: Given an input string (s) and a pattern (p), implement wildcard pattern matching with support for '?' and '*' where '?' matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters (including the empty sequence).
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
p contains only lowercase English letters, '?' or '*'.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement regular expression matching with support for '.' and '*' where '.' matches any single character, and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
p contains only lowercase English letters, '.', and '*'.
For each appearance of '*', there will be a valid preceding character to match.

title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
description: Given an m x n grid. Each cell has a sign pointing right, left, down, or up. You can modify the sign of a cell with cost = 1. Return the minimum cost to make at least one valid path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell.

title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of good subarrays of nums. A good array is an array where the number of different integers in that array is exactly k.

title: Swim in Rising Water
description: You are given an n x n integer matrix grid where each value grid[i][j] represents the elevation at that point (i, j). Rain starts falling at time 0. At time t, the water depth everywhere is t. Return the least time until you can reach the bottom-right square starting from the top-left square.
constraints: Each value in grid is unique.

title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
description: You have an undirected, connected graph of n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1. You are given an array graph where graph[i] is a list of all the nodes connected with node i by an edge. Return the length of the shortest path that visits every node.
constraints: If graph[a] contains b, then graph[b] contains a.

title: Sum of Distances in Tree
description: There is an undirected connected tree with n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1 and n - 1 edges. You are given the integer n and the array edges where edges[i] = [ai, bi] indicates that there is an edge between nodes ai and bi in the tree. Return an array ans of length n where ans[i] is the sum of the distances between the ith node and all other nodes in the tree.
constraints: The given input represents a valid tree.

title: Trapping Rain Water II
description: Given an m x n integer matrix heightMap representing the height of each unit cell in a 2D elevation map, return the volume of water it can trap after raining.

title: Burst Balloons
description: You are given n balloons, indexed from 0 to n - 1. Each balloon is painted with a number on it represented by an array nums. You are asked to burst all the balloons. If you burst the ith balloon, you will get nums[i - 1] * nums[i] * nums[i + 1] coins. Return the maximum coins you can collect by bursting the balloons wisely.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Serialization is the process of converting a data structure or object into a sequence of bits so that it can be stored in a file or memory buffer, or transmitted across a network connection link to be reconstructed later in the same or another computer environment. Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].

title: 24 Game
description: You are given an integer array cards of length 4. You have four cards, each containing a number in the range [1, 9]. You should arrange the numbers on these cards in a mathematical expression using the operators ['+', '-', '*', '/'] and the parentheses '(' and ')' to get the value 24. Return true if you can get such expression that evaluates to 24, or false otherwise.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
description: Given an m x n integers matrix, return the length of the longest increasing path in matrix. From each cell, you can either move in four directions: left, right, up, or down. You may not move diagonally or move outside the boundary.

title: Height of Binary Tree After Subtree Removal Queries
description: You are given the root of a binary tree with n nodes, and an array queries of size m. For each query, remove the subtree rooted at queries[i] from the tree and find the height of the remaining tree. Return an array of size m containing the answer for each query.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is n.
All the values in the tree are unique.

title: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, calculate the vertical order traversal of the binary tree. For each node at position (row, col), its left and right children will be at (row + 1, col - 1) and (row + 1, col + 1) respectively. Report the nodes row-by-row and sorted by value from top to bottom.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000].

title: Permutation Sequence
description: The set [1, 2, 3, ..., n] contains a total of n! unique permutations. By listing and labeling all of the permutations in order, given n and k, return the kth permutation sequence.

title: Meeting Rooms III
description: You are given an integer n representing n rooms numbered from 0 to n - 1. You are given a 2D integer array meetings where meetings[i] = [starti, endi] means that a meeting will be held during the half-closed time interval [starti, endi). Return the number of the room that held the most meetings.

title: LFU Cache
description: Design and implement a data structure for a Least Frequently Used (LFU) cache. Implement the LFUCache class with get(key) and put(key, value) operations. When the cache reaches its capacity, it should invalidate and remove the least frequently used key before inserting a new item.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^5 calls will be made to get and put.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Given two strings s and t of lengths m and n respectively, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. If there is no such substring, return the empty string "".
constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters.

title: Bus Routes
description: You are given an array routes representing bus routes where routes[i] is a bus route that the ith bus repeats forever. You start at the bus stop source and want to go to the bus stop target. Return the least number of buses you must take to travel from source to target, or -1 if it is not possible.
constraints: All elements of routes[i] are unique.

title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
description: You are given an m x n integer matrix grid where each cell is either 0 (empty) or 1 (obstacle). You can move up, down, left, or right from and to an empty cell. You can eliminate at most k obstacles. Return the minimum number of steps to walk from the upper left corner to the lower right corner.

title: Word Ladder
description: A transformation sequence from word beginWord to word endWord using a dictionary wordList is a sequence of words beginWord -> s1 -> s2 -> ... -> sk such that every adjacent pair of words differs by a single letter, and every si is in wordList. Return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, or 0 if no such sequence exists.
constraints: beginWord, endWord, and wordList[i] consist of lowercase English letters.
All words in wordList are unique.

title: The Skyline Problem
description: A city's skyline is the outer contour of the silhouette formed by all the buildings in that city when viewed from a distance. Given the locations and heights of all the buildings, return the skyline formed by these buildings collectively.
constraints: buildings is sorted by lefti in non-decreasing order.

title: Range Module
description: A Range Module is a module that tracks ranges of numbers. Design and implement an algorithm to track half-open intervals and query/remove them.
constraints: At most 10^4 calls will be made to addRange, queryRange, and removeRange.

title: Race Car
description: Your car starts at position 0 and speed +1 on an infinite number line. Your car can go into negative positions. An instruction sequence of 'A' (accelerate) and 'R' (reverse) drives your car. Given a target position target, return the length of the shortest sequence of instructions to get there.

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
description: You are given a list of airline tickets where tickets[i] = [fromi, toi] represent the departure and the arrival airports of one flight. Reconstruct the itinerary in order and return it. All tickets belong to a man whose departure is 'JFK'.
constraints: fromi and toi consist of uppercase English letters.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description: Given an integer array nums, return an integer array counts where counts[i] is the number of smaller elements to the right of nums[i].

title: Expression Add Operators
description: Given a string num that contains only digits and an integer target, return all possibilities to insert the binary operators '+', '-', and/or '*' between the digits of num so that the resultant expression evaluates to the target value.

title: Minimum Time to Finish the Race
description: You are given a 2D integer array tires where tires[i] = [fi, ri] indicates that the ith tire can finish its xth lap in fi * ri^(x-1) seconds. You are also given an integer changeTime representing the time to change tires and numLaps representing the number of laps. Return the minimum time to complete the race.

title: Shortest Palindrome
description: You are given a string s. You can convert s to a palindrome by adding characters in front of it. Return the shortest palindrome you can find by performing this transformation.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only.

title: Minimum Weighted Subgraph With the Required Paths
description: You are given an integer n representing nodes in a directed weighted graph, a 2D array edges, and three distinct nodes src1, src2, and dest. Return the minimum weight of a subgraph such that there is a path from src1 to dest and from src2 to dest. If no such subgraph exists, return -1.
constraints: 0 <= fromi, toi, src1, src2, dest <= n - 1
src1, src2, and dest are pairwise distinct.

title: Odd Even Jump
description: You are given an integer array arr. From some starting index, you can make a series of jumps alternating between odd-numbered jumps (jumps to the smallest element that is greater than or equal to current) and even-numbered jumps (jumps to the largest element that is less than or equal to current). Return the number of good starting indices from which you can reach the end of the array.

title: Number of Islands II
description: You are given an empty 2D binary grid of size m x n and an array positions where positions[i] = [ri, ci] turns water into land at (ri, ci). Return an array of integers representing the number of islands after each operation.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string containing just the characters '(' and ')', return the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.

title: Finding MK Average
description: You are given two integers, m and k, and a stream of integers. Implement the MKAverage class that maintains the stream and calculates the MK Average: the average of the last m elements after removing the smallest k and largest k elements, rounded down to the nearest integer.
constraints: At most 10^5 calls will be made to addElement and calculateMKAverage.

title: Word Search II
description: Given an m x n board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words on the board. Each word must be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring.
constraints: board[i][j] is a lowercase English letter.
words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All strings in words are unique.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
description: A string is beautiful if it consists of the first k English lowercase letters and does not contain any palindromic substrings of length 2 or more. Given a beautiful string s and an integer k, return the lexicographically smallest beautiful string of length n that is larger than s. If no such string exists, return an empty string.

title: Alien Dictionary
description: There is a new alien language that uses the English alphabet. You are given a list of strings words from the alien language's dictionary, where the strings are claimed to be sorted lexicographically by the rules of this new language. Return a string of the unique letters in the new alien language sorted in lexicographically increasing order. If the order is invalid, return "".
constraints: words[i] consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Integer to English Words
description: Convert a non-negative integer num to its English words representation.

examples.output: "One Million Two Hundred Thirty Four Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Seven"

title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
description: You are given a string s and an array of strings words. All the strings of words are of the same length. Return an array of the starting indices of all the concatenated substrings in s that contain each string in words exactly once, without any intervening characters.
constraints: s and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Next Special Palindrome Number
description: Given a positive integer n, return the smallest special palindrome number strictly greater than n. A special palindrome is defined as a numeric palindrome whose digits satisfy specific parity and symmetry rules.

title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
description: You are given an integer array nums of 2 * n integers. You need to partition nums into two arrays of length n to minimize the absolute difference of the sums of the arrays. Return the minimum possible absolute difference.

title: Unique Paths III
description: You are given an m x n integer array grid where 1 represents starting square, 2 represents ending square, 0 represents empty square, and -1 represents obstacle. Return the number of 4-directional walks from the starting square to the ending square, that walk over every non-obstacle square exactly once.
constraints: There is one starting square and one ending square.

title: Build a Matrix With Conditions
description: You are given a positive integer k and two 2D integer arrays rowConditions and colConditions. Return a k x k matrix containing each number from 1 to k exactly once, such that all row and column order constraints are satisfied. If no such matrix exists, return an empty matrix.

title: N-Queens II
description: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Given an integer n, return the number of distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle.

title: Find the Subtasks That Did Not Execute
description: Write a solution to report the IDs of the subtasks for each task_id that were not executed. Return the result table in any order.

title: Robot Room Cleaner
description: You are controlling a robot located in an unknown room with obstacles. The robot can move forward, turn left, turn right, and clean the current space. Clean the entire room using only the Robot API.

title: Painting a Grid With Three Different Colors
description: You are given two integers m and n. Consider an m x n grid where each cell is painted with one of three colors: Red, Green, or Blue. No two adjacent cells may have the same color. Return the number of valid ways to paint the grid modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximum Number of K-Divisible Components
description: There is an undirected tree with n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1. You are given n, a 2D array edges, an integer array values, and an integer k. Return the maximum number of components in any valid split such that the sum of the values of the nodes in each component is divisible by k.
constraints: The input is guaranteed to form a valid tree.

title: Employee Free Time
description: We are given a list schedule of employees, which represents the working time for each employee. Return the list of finite intervals representing common, positive-length free time for all employees, sorted in increasing order.

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted III
description: You are given an array of n strings strs, all of the same length. We may choose any deletion indices and delete all characters in those indices from each string. Return the minimum number of deletion indices such that every remaining string is lexicographically sorted.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Cherry Pickup II
description: You are given a rows x cols matrix grid representing a field of cherries. Two robots start at (0, 0) and (0, cols - 1). Return the maximum number of cherries collection both robots can collect following the movement rules until reaching the bottom row.

title: Minimum Distance to Type a Word Using Two Fingers
description: You have a 2-finger keyboard layout where English uppercase letters are arranged in a 6 x 5 grid. Given a string word, return the minimum total distance to type the string using two fingers starting at any position.
constraints: word consists of only uppercase English letters.

title: The Earliest and Latest Rounds Where Players Compete
description: There is a tournament with n players numbered 1 to n. In each round, players pair up from outer ends (1 vs n, 2 vs n-1, etc.). The two players with ranks firstPlayer and secondPlayer always win their matches against anyone else. Return an integer array containing the earliest and latest possible round in which firstPlayer and secondPlayer compete against each other.

title: My Calendar III
description: A k-booking happens when k events have some non-empty intersection. Implement the MyCalendarThree class that calculates the largest k-booking among all booked events.
constraints: At most 400 calls will be made to book.

title: Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
description: You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array grid of size m x n. Each cell has a value 0 (empty) or 1 (obstacle). Return the minimum number of obstacles to remove so you can move from (0, 0) to (m - 1, n - 1).

title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
description: You have k lists of sorted integers in non-decreasing order. Find the smallest range that includes at least one number from each of the k lists.
constraints: nums[i] is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Minimize Maximum Value in a Grid
description: You are given an m x n integer matrix grid containing distinct positive integers. You have to replace each integer in the matrix with a positive integer such that the relative order of elements in every row and column remains the same, and the maximum number in the modified grid is minimized. Return the modified matrix.
constraints: All elements in grid are distinct.

title: Parsing A Boolean Expression
description: A boolean expression is an expression that evaluates to either true or false. Given a string expression that represents a boolean expression, return the evaluation of that expression. Supported operators are !(subExpr), &(subExpr1, subExpr2, ...), and |(subExpr1, subExpr2, ...).

title: Shortest Impossible Sequence of Rolls
description: You are given an integer array rolls of length n and an integer k. You roll a k-sided dice n times, where the results are given by rolls. Return the length of the shortest sequence of rolls that cannot be taken from rolls as a subsequence.

title: Last Day Where You Can Still Cross
description: There is a 1-based binary matrix where 0 represents land and 1 represents water. You are given row and col, and an array cells where cells[i] = [ri, ci] represents that on the ith day, the cell at (ri, ci) becomes water. Return the last day where it is possible to walk from the top row to the bottom row by only walking on land cells.
constraints: All values of cells are unique.

title: Parallel Courses III
description: You are given an integer n, which indicates that there are n courses labeled from 1 to n. You are also given a 2D integer array relations and an integer array time where time[i] denotes the number of months required to complete the (i+1)th course. Find the minimum number of months needed to complete all the courses respecting prerequisites, assuming you can take any number of courses simultaneously.
constraints: The prerequisite graph is a directed acyclic graph.

title: Count Fertile Pyramids in a Land
description: A farmer has a rectangular grid of land with values 0 (barren) and 1 (fertile). A pyramidal plot of height h has an apex and spans symmetrically downwards, while an inverse pyramidal plot spans upwards. Return the total number of pyramidal and inverse pyramidal plots of height >= 2 in the land.

title: Median Employee Salary
description: Write a solution to find the median salary of each company. If there are an even number of employees, report both middle salary entries.
constraints: id is the primary key column for the table.
Each row of this table indicates the company and the salary of an employee.

title: Optimize Water Distribution in a Village
description: There are n houses in a village. You can either build a well inside the house at cost wells[i - 1] or connect house i to house j with a pipe at cost pipes[j][2]. Return the minimum total cost to supply water to all houses.

title: Divide Array Into Increasing Sequences
description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer k, return true if you can divide the array into one or more strictly increasing subsequences such that each sequence has a length of at least k.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Number of Atoms
description: Given a string formula representing a chemical formula, return the count of each atom. Return the count of all elements as a string sorted in alphabetical order.
constraints: formula consists of English letters, digits, '(', and ')'.

title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People II
description: You are given a 2D array points of size n x 2 where points[i] = [xi, yi]. Alice and Bob want to choose two points (A, B) such that A is on the upper left side of B and no other points lie inside or on the boundary of the rectangle formed with A as upper-left and B as lower-right. Return the number of pairs of points they can choose.

title: Maximum Score of a Good Subarray
description: You are given an array of integers nums and an integer k. The score of a subarray (i, j) is defined as min(nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[j]) * (j - i + 1). A good subarray is a subarray where i <= k <= j. Return the maximum possible score of a good subarray.

title: Design Video Sharing Platform
description: Design a video sharing platform where users can upload videos, watch videos, like/dislike videos, and query the view, like, and dislike counts of a video.
constraints: At most 10^5 calls will be made in total across all functions.

title: Count Ways to Distribute Candies
description: There are n unique candies and k identical bags. You want to distribute all the candies into the bags such that every bag contains at least one candy. Return the number of different ways to distribute the candies modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Brace Expansion II
description: Under the grammar given in the problem, return the list of words formed by evaluating the expression, sorted in lexicographical order with duplicates removed.
constraints: expression[i] consists of '{', '}', ',', or lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
description: There are n workers. You are given two integer arrays quality and wage where quality[i] is the quality of the ith worker and wage[i] is the minimum wage expectation. Given an integer k, return the least amount of money needed to form a paid group of k workers subject to wage ratio rules.

title: Stone Game III
description: Alice and Bob continue their games with piles of stones. There are several stones arranged in a row. On each player's turn, that player can take 1, 2, or 3 stones from the remaining stones. Determine if Alice wins, Bob wins, or it's a Tie assuming optimal play.

title: Checking Existence of Edge Length Limited Paths
description: An undirected graph of n nodes is given with edge list. You are also given queries where queries[j] = [pj, qj, limitj]. Return a boolean array answer where answer[j] is true if there exists a path between pj and qj such that each edge on the path has a distance strictly less than limitj.

title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
description: Given a wooden stick of length n and an array cuts where cuts[i] denotes a position where you should perform a cut. The cost of one cut is the length of the stick to be cut. Return the minimum total cost of the cuts.
constraints: All the integers in cuts are distinct.

title: Minimum Falling Path Sum II
description: Given an n x n integer matrix grid, return the minimum sum of a falling path with non-zero shifts such that no two elements in consecutive rows are in the same column.

title: Word Abbreviation
description: Given an array of distinct strings words, return the minimal possible abbreviations for every word following the given abbreviation rules without ambiguity.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All strings of words are unique.

title: Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K
description: The score of an array is defined as the product of its sum and its length. Given a positive integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of non-empty subarrays of nums whose score is strictly less than k.

title: Shortest Common Supersequence
description: Given two strings str1 and str2, return the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences. If there are multiple valid strings, return any of them.
constraints: str1 and str2 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Number of Ways to Rearrange Sticks With K Sticks Visible
description: There are n uniquely-sized sticks whose lengths are integers from 1 to n. You want to arrange them such that exactly k sticks are visible from the left. A stick is visible from the left if there are no longer sticks to the left of it. Return the number of such arrangements modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximum Employees to Be Invited to a Meeting
description: A company is organizing a meeting and has a list of n employees, each employee has a single favorite person they want to sit next to. Employees will only attend if they can sit next to their favorite person at a round table. Return the maximum number of employees that can be invited to the meeting.

title: Number of Ways of Cutting a Pizza
description: Given a rectangular pizza represented as a rows x cols matrix of characters where 'A' represents an apple and '.' represents an empty cell, and an integer k. In each cut you can choose to cut either horizontally or vertically into two pieces and give the piece with at least one apple to a person. Return the number of ways of cutting the pizza such that each of the k pieces has at least one apple, modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Closest Binary Search Tree Value II
description: Given the root of a binary search tree, a target value, and an integer k, return the k values in the BST that are closest to the target. You may return the answer in any order.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is n.

title: Strange Printer II
description: Given a grid of size m x n where each cell has a color. In each turn, the printer can print a solid rectangular pattern of a single color over the grid. Return true if it is possible to print the given grid from a blank canvas, or false otherwise.

title: Smallest Rectangle Enclosing Black Pixels
description: You are given an m x n binary matrix image where 0 represents a white pixel and 1 represents a black pixel. All black pixels are 4-way connected. Given the location of one black pixel (x, y), return the area of the smallest (axis-aligned) rectangle that encloses all black pixels.

title: Process Restricted Friend Requests
description: You are given an integer n indicating the number of people in a network, labeled from 0 to n - 1. You are given a 2D array restrictions where restrictions[i] = [xi, yi] means that person xi and person yi cannot be friends directly or indirectly. You are also given a 2D array requests where requests[j] = [uj, vj]. Return a boolean array result where result[j] is true if the jth request can be accepted without violating restrictions, and false otherwise.

title: Sum of Prefix Scores of Strings
description: You are given an array words of size n consisting of non-empty strings. Define the score of a string word as the number of strings in words that have word as a prefix. Return an array answer of size n where answer[i] is the sum of scores of every non-empty prefix of words[i].
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Divide Chocolate
description: You have one chocolate bar that consists of some chunks. Each chunk has its own sweetness given by the array sweetness. You want to share the chocolate with your k friends by making k cuts to divide the chocolate bar into k + 1 pieces. Return the maximum total sweetness of the piece you can get after dividing the chocolate bar optimally.

title: Maximum Value of K Coins From Piles
description: There are n piles of coins on a table. In one move, you can choose any pile and take the top coin from it. Given piles where piles[i] is a list of integers from top to bottom and an integer k, return the maximum total value of coins you can have in your wallet if you can take at most k coins.

title: Number of Stable Subsequences
description: You are given an integer array nums. A subsequence is called stable if it satisfies the stability conditions defined on its adjacent differences and parity. Return the total number of stable subsequences modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Critical Connections in a Network
description: There are n servers numbered 0 to n - 1 connected by undirected server-to-server connections forming a network. A critical connection is a connection that, if removed, will make some servers unable to reach some other server. Return all critical connections in the network in any order.

title: Maximum Sum of 3 Non-Overlapping Subarrays
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find three non-overlapping subarrays of length k with maximum resulting sum and return the starting indices of the subarrays. If there are multiple answers, return the lexicographically smallest one.

title: Design Skiplist
description: Design a Skiplist without using any built-in libraries. Implement the Skiplist class supporting search(target), add(num), and erase(num) in O(log(n)) expected time.

examples.output: [null, null, null, null, false, null, true, false, true, false]

constraints: At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to search, add, and erase.

title: Move Sub-Tree of N-Ary Tree
description: Given the root of an N-ary tree and two nodes p and q in the tree. Move the subtree with root p to be a child of q. If p is an ancestor of q, make q a child of p's parent first before attaching p to q. Return the root of the modified tree.
constraints: The total number of nodes is between [2, 1000].
Each node has a unique value.

title: Couples Holding Hands
description: There are n couples sitting in 2n seats arranged in a row and want to hold hands. The people and seats are represented by an integer array row of length 2n where row[i] is the person sitting in the ith seat. Return the minimum number of swaps so that every couple is sitting side by side.

title: The Most Similar Path in a Graph
description: We have n cities and m bidirectional roads connecting them. You are given a target path targetPath of length k. Return a path in the graph of length k that minimizes the edit distance with targetPath.

title: Freedom Trail
description: In the video game Fallout 4, the quest "Road to Freedom" requires players to reach a metal dial called the "Freedom Trail Ring" and use the dial to spell a specific keyword. Given strings ring and key, return the minimum number of steps to spell all the characters in the keyword.
constraints: ring and key consist of lowercase English letters.
It is guaranteed that key could always be spelled by rotating ring.

title: Separate Squares II
description: You are given a 2D integer array squares where squares[i] = [xi, yi, li] represents the coordinates of the bottom-left point and the side length of the ith square. Find the minimum y-coordinate of a horizontal line such that the total area of the squares above the line equals the total area below the line.

title: Longest Chunked Palindrome Decomposition
description: You are given a string text. You should split it into k substrings (subtext1, subtext2, ..., subtextk) such that subtexti == subtextk - i + 1 for all valid i. Return the largest possible value of k.
constraints: text consists only of lowercase English characters.

title: Maximum XOR With an Element From Array
description: You are given an array nums consisting of non-negative integers. You are also given a queries array, where queries[j] = [xj, mj]. Return an array answer where answer[j] is the maximum bitwise XOR value of xj with any element of nums that does not exceed mj. If all elements in nums exceed mj, then answer[j] = -1.

title: Paths in Matrix Whose Sum Is Divisible by K
description: You are given a 0-indexed m x n integer matrix grid and an integer k. You are currently at (0, 0) and you want to reach (m - 1, n - 1) moving only down or right. Return the number of paths where the sum of elements along the path is divisible by k modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Cracking the Safe
description: There is a safe protected by a password with n digits where each digit is one of the first k digits 0, 1, ..., k - 1. Return any string of minimum length that is guaranteed to open the safe after the entire string is typed.

title: Car Fleet II
description: There are n cars traveling at different positions in the same direction along a one-lane road. You are given an array cars, where cars[i] = [positioni, speedi]. A car can never pass another car ahead of it, but it can catch up to it and drive bumper to bumper at the same speed (forming a car fleet). Return an array answer, where answer[i] is the time at which the ith car collides with the next car, or -1 if the car does not collide with the next car.

title: Number of Flowers in Full Bloom
description: You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array flowers, where flowers[i] = [starti, endi] means the ith flower will be in full bloom from starti to endi (inclusive). You are also given a 0-indexed integer array people of size n, where people[i] is the time that the ith person will arrive to see the flowers. Return an integer array answer of size n, where answer[i] is the number of flowers that are in full bloom when the ith person arrives.

title: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph
description: There is a directed graph of n colored nodes and m edges. The nodes are numbered from 0 to n - 1. You are given a string colors of length n, where colors[i] is a lowercase English letter representing the color of the ith node. You are also given a 2D array edges where edges[j] = [uj, vj] indicates a directed edge from uj to vj. Return the largest color value of any valid path in the graph, or -1 if the graph contains a cycle.
constraints: colors consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Flips in Binary Tree to Get Result
description: You are given the root of a binary tree with the following properties: Leaf nodes have either the value 0 or 1. Non-leaf nodes have the value 2 (OR), 3 (AND), 4 (XOR), or 5 (NOT). You are also given a boolean result. In one operation, you can flip the value of a leaf node (0 to 1, or 1 to 0). Return the minimum number of operations needed so that the tree evaluates to result.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^5].

title: Making A Large Island
description: You are given an n x n binary matrix grid. You are allowed to change at most one 0 to be 1. Return the size of the largest island in grid after applying this operation. An island is a 4-directionally connected group of 1s.

title: Student Attendance Record II
description: An attendance record for a student can be represented as a string where each character signifies whether the student was absent, late, or present. An attendance record is eligible for an award if it contains strictly fewer than 2 'A' (absent) characters and never contains 3 or more consecutive 'L' (late) characters. Given an integer n, return the number of possible award-eligible attendance records of length n modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Number of Good Paths
description: There is a tree consisting of n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1. You are given a 0-indexed integer array vals of length n, where vals[i] denotes the value of the ith node. You are also given a 2D integer array edges. A good path is a simple path where the starting and ending nodes have the same value, and all intermediate nodes have values less than or equal to the starting node. Return the number of distinct good paths.

title: Similar String Groups
description: Two strings X and Y are similar if they are equal or if we can swap two letters in X to produce Y. Given a list of anagrams strs, group similar strings into connected components and return the total number of connected components.
constraints: All words in strs have the same length and are anagrams of each other.

title: Word Break II
description: Given a string s and a dictionary of strings wordDict, add spaces in s to construct a sentence where each word is a valid dictionary word. Return all such possible sentences in any order.

examples.output: ["pine apple pen apple","pineapple pen apple","pine applepen apple"]

constraints: s and wordDict[i] consist of only lowercase English letters.
All strings in wordDict are unique.

title: Amount of New Area Painted Each Day
description: There is a 1D painting that is initially unpainted. You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array paint of length n, where paint[i] = [starti, endi] indicates that on the ith day you need to paint the interval [starti, endi]. Return an integer array worklog of length n, where worklog[i] is the amount of new area painted on the ith day.

title: Tiling a Rectangle with the Fewest Squares
description: Given a rectangle of size n x m, find the minimum number of integer-sided squares required to tile the rectangle completely.

title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted II
description: You are given an integer array arr. We split arr into some number of chunks (i.e., partitions), and individually sort each chunk. After concatenating them, the result should equal the sorted array. Return the maximum number of chunks we can make to sort the array.

title: Shortest Path to Get All Keys
description: You are given an m x n grid where '.' is an empty cell, '#' is a wall, '@' is the start position, lowercase letters 'a'-'f' represent keys, and uppercase letters 'A'-'F' represent locks. Return the lowest number of moves to acquire all keys, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: grid[i][j] is '.', '#', '@', lowercase English letters ('a'-'f'), or uppercase English letters ('A'-'F').
The number of keys in the grid is in the range [1, 6].
Each key and lock pair is unique.
There is exactly one start point '@'.

title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
description: We have n jobs, where every job is scheduled to run from startTime[i] to endTime[i], yielding profit[i]. Return the maximum profit you can achieve without scheduling overlapping jobs.

title: Word Squares
description: Given an array of unique strings words, return all word squares you can build from words. You can use the same word multiple times, and each word has the same length. A sequence of words forms a valid word square if the kth row and column read the exact same string.
constraints: All words[i] have the same length.
words[i] consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
description: You are given a 2D integer array intervals where intervals[i] = [lefti, righti]. The size of an interval is defined as righti - lefti + 1. You are also given an integer array queries. Return an array ans where ans[j] is the minimum size of an interval containing queries[j], or -1 if no such interval exists.

title: Patching Array
description: Given a sorted integer array nums and an integer n, add/patch the minimum number of elements to nums such that any number in the range [1, n] inclusive can be formed by the sum of some elements in the array. Return the minimum number of patches required.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order.

title: Kth Smallest Number in Multiplication Table
description: The multiplication table of size m x n is an integer matrix mat where mat[i][j] == i * j (1-indexed). Given three integers m, n, and k, return the kth smallest element in the m x n multiplication table.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
description: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. Find the maximum profit you can achieve with at most two transactions. You must sell before buying again.

title: Number of Ways to Reorder Array to Get Same BST
description: Given an array nums that represents a permutation of integers from 1 to n. We construct a binary search tree (BST) by inserting elements of nums sequentially. Find the number of different permutations of nums that yield the identical BST structure modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: All integers in nums are distinct.

title: Pizza With 3n Slices
description: There is a circular pizza with 3n slices. You and your two friends take turns picking slices: you pick any slice, and your friends pick adjacent slices. Return the maximum possible sum of slice sizes that you can collect.

title: Top Three Wineries
description: Write a solution to find the top three wineries in each country based on their total points. In case of ties, order wineries alphabetically by name. Return the result table ordered by country in ascending order.

title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
description: You are given an integer array stations representing gas station positions on the x-axis. You must add k new gas stations anywhere on the x-axis. Return the minimum possible maximum distance between adjacent gas stations after adding k stations.
constraints: stations is sorted in strictly increasing order.

title: Maximum Frequency of an Element After Performing Operations II
description: You are given an integer array nums and integers k and numOperations. You can perform at most numOperations operations where in each operation you can increment or decrement any nums[i] by at most k. Return the maximum possible frequency of any element in nums.

title: Longest Happy Prefix
description: A string is called a happy prefix if it is a non-empty prefix that is also a suffix (excluding the full string itself). Given a string s, return the longest happy prefix of s, or empty string "" if none exists.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.

title: Basic Calculator III
description: Implement a basic calculator to evaluate a simple expression string containing non-negative integers, '+', '-', '*', '/' operators, and parentheses '(' and ')'.

title: Distinct Echo Substrings
description: Return the number of distinct non-empty substrings of text that can be written as the concatenation of some string with itself (i.e., a + a).
constraints: text has only lowercase English letters.

title: Erect the Fence
description: You are given an array trees where trees[i] = [xi, yi] represents the location of a tree. Return the coordinates of trees that are exactly located on the convex perimeter fence that encloses all trees.

title: Stream of Characters
description: Design an algorithm that accepts a stream of characters and checks if any suffix of these characters matches a word in a given list of strings words.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
letter is a lowercase English letter.
At most 4 * 10^4 calls will be made to query.

title: Longest Common Suffix Queries
description: You are given two string arrays wordsContainer and wordsQuery. For each wordsQuery[i], find the string from wordsContainer that has the longest common suffix with wordsQuery[i]. If there is a tie, choose the string with the minimum length. If there is still a tie, choose the string that occurred earlier in wordsContainer. Return an array of integers representing the index of each string.
constraints: wordsContainer[i] and wordsQuery[i] consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Number of Unique Good Subsequences
description: You are given a binary string binary. A subsequence of binary is considered good if it is not empty and has no leading zeros (except for the string "0" itself). Return the number of unique good subsequences of binary modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Distinct Subsequences
description: Given two strings s and t, return the number of distinct subsequences of s which equals t.
constraints: s and t consist of English letters.

title: Check If String Is Transformable With Substring Sort Operations
description: Given two strings s and t, transform s into t using the following operation: choose a non-empty substring of s and sort it in ascending order. Return true if you can transform s into t, or false otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of only digits.

title: Transform to Chessboard
description: You are given an n x n binary grid board. In each move, you can swap any two rows, or any two columns. Return the minimum number of moves to transform the board into a chessboard board, or -1 if it is impossible.

title: Checking Existence of Edge Length Limited Paths II
description: An undirected graph of n nodes is given with a list of edge weights. Implement DistanceLimitedPathsExist class with query(p, q, limit) returning true if there is a path from p to q such that every edge on the path has a distance strictly less than limit.
constraints: At most 10^4 calls will be made to query.

title: Erect the Fence II
description: You are given a 2D integer array trees where trees[i] = [xi, yi] represents the location of a tree in the garden. You want to build a circular fence that encloses all the trees. Return the center (x, y) and radius r of the smallest circle that encloses all the trees.

title: Design a Text Editor
description: Design a text editor with a cursor that can add text, delete text, and move the cursor left and right. Implement the TextEditor class.
constraints: text consists of lowercase English letters.
At most 2 * 10^4 calls in total will be made to addText, deleteText, cursorLeft, and cursorRight.

title: Jump Game IV
description: Given an array of integers arr, you are initially positioned at the first index of the array. In one step you can jump from index i to i + 1, i - 1, or j where arr[i] == arr[j] and i != j. Return the minimum number of steps to reach the last index of the array.

title: Maximum AND Sum of Array
description: You are given an integer array nums of length n and an integer numSlots such that 2 * numSlots >= n. There are numSlots slots numbered from 1 to numSlots. Put all integers into slots such that each slot contains at most two integers. The AND sum is the sum of (nums[i] AND slot_number). Return the maximum possible AND sum.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
description: You are given an integer array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on the ith day, and an integer k. Find the maximum profit you can achieve with at most k transactions. You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously.

title: Encode String with Shortest Length
description: Given a string s, encode the string such that its encoded length is the shortest. The encoding rule is: k[encoded_string] where the encoded_string inside the square brackets is being repeated exactly k times.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Optimal Account Balancing
description: You are given an array of transactions transactions where transactions[i] = [fromi, toi, amounti] indicates that the person with ID fromi gave amounti $ to person toi. Return the minimum number of transactions required to settle all debts.

title: Minimum Cost to Connect Two Groups of Points
description: You are given two groups of points where the first group has size1 points and the second group has size2 points. The cost to connect point i in the first group and point j in the second group is cost[i][j]. Return the minimum cost to connect both groups such that each point is connected to at least one point in the other group.

title: Time Taken to Cross the Door
description: There are n persons who want to cross a door either entering or exiting. Given arrival, state, and door usage rules, return an array answer of size n where answer[i] is the time at which the ith person crossed the door.
constraints: arrival is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps
description: You have a pointer at index 0 in an array of size arrLen. In each step, you can move 1 position to the left, 1 position to the right, or stay in the same place. Return the number of ways to stay at index 0 after exactly steps steps modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Design Search Autocomplete System
description: Design a search autocomplete system for a search engine. Users can input a sentence character by character. Implement AutocompleteSystem class to return the top 3 historical hot sentences that have the same prefix.

examples.output: [null, ["i love you", "island", "i love leetcode"], ["i love you", "i love leetcode"], [], []]

constraints: c is a lowercase English letter, ' ', or '#'.
At most 5000 calls will be made to input.

title: Count the Number of Good Partitions
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums. A partition is good if no two occurrences of the same number appear in different subarrays. Return the total number of good partitions modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Form Largest Integer With Digits That Add up to Target
description: Given an integer array cost and an integer target, return the maximum integer you can paint under the rules such that total cost equals target. If no integer can be painted, return "0".

title: Minimum Operations to Make a Subsequence
description: You are given an array target consisting of distinct integers and an integer array arr that can contain duplicates. Return the minimum number of operations to make target a subsequence of arr (where an operation inserts an integer anywhere).

title: Minimum Cost to Change the Final Value of Expression
description: You are given a valid boolean expression s consisting of '0', '1', '&', '|', '(', and ')'. Return the minimum cost to change the final value of the expression.
constraints: s is valid and contains only '0', '1', '&', '|', '(', and ')'.

title: Count Subarrays With Median K
description: You are given an array nums of size n consisting of distinct integers from 1 to n and a positive integer k. Return the number of non-empty subarrays that have a median equal to k.
constraints: All integers in nums are distinct.

title: Kth Smallest Product of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2 and an integer k, return the kth (1-based) smallest product of nums1[i] * nums2[j] where 0 <= i < nums1.length and 0 <= j < nums2.length.

title: Profitable Schemes
description: There is a group of n members, and a list of crimes. Given n, minProfit, group, and profit, return the number of schemes that can be chosen and generate at least minProfit profit modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Find All People With Secret
description: You are given an integer n indicating there are n people labeled from 0 to n - 1. You are also given a 2D integer array meetings where meetings[i] = [xi, yi, timei] and an integer firstPerson. Person 0 has a secret and shares it with firstPerson at time 0. Secret sharing happens instantaneously in simultaneous meetings. Return a list of all people who know the secret after all meetings.

title: Numbers With Repeated Digits
description: Given a positive integer n, return the number of positive integers in the range [1, n] that have at least one repeated digit.

title: Find the Count of Monotonic Pairs I
description: You are given an array of positive integers nums of length n. A pair of non-negative integer arrays (arr1, arr2) of length n is called monotonic if arr1 is monotonically non-decreasing, arr2 is monotonically non-increasing, and arr1[i] + arr2[i] == nums[i] for all 0 <= i <= n - 1. Return the count of monotonic pairs modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Number of Pairs Satisfying Inequality
description: You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2, each of size n, and an integer diff. Find the number of pairs (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j <= n - 1 and nums1[i] - nums1[j] <= nums2[i] - nums2[j] + diff.

title: Frog Jump
description: A frog is crossing a river divided into units with stones placed at some locations. The frog is initially on the first stone and jumps 1 unit to the second stone. If the frog's last jump was k units, its next jump must be either k - 1, k, or k + 1 units. Return true if the frog can land on the last stone, or false otherwise.
constraints: stones is sorted in a strictly increasing order.

title: Confusing Number II
description: A confusing number is a number that when rotated 180 degrees becomes a different number with each digit valid (0, 1, 6, 8, 9). Given an integer n, return the number of confusing numbers in the inclusive range [1, n].

title: Maximum Vacation Days
description: LeetCode wants to give one of its best employees the option to travel among n cities to take vacations. You are given an n x n matrix flights representing flight connections between cities, and an n x k matrix days where days[i][j] represents the maximum vacation days you can take in city i during week j. Return the maximum vacation days you could take during k weeks starting at city 0.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
description: Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. Given the sorted rotated array nums that may contain duplicates, return the minimum element of this array.
constraints: nums is sorted and rotated between 1 and n times.

title: Find K-th Smallest Pair Distance
description: The distance of a pair of integers a and b is defined as the absolute difference |a - b|. Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth smallest distance among all the pairs nums[i] and nums[j] where 0 <= i < j < nums.length.

title: Smallest Good Base
description: Given an integer n represented as a string, return the smallest good base of n. We call k >= 2 a good base of n if all digits of n base k are 1.
constraints: n is an integer in the range [3, 10^18].
n does not contain any leading zeros.

title: Minimum Time to Build Blocks
description: You are given a list of blocks, where blocks[i] = t means that the ith block needs t units of time to be built. One worker can split into two workers in split units of time, and each worker can only build one block at a time. Return the minimum time needed to build all blocks.

title: K-th Smallest in Lexicographical Order
description: Given two integers n and k, return the kth lexicographically smallest integer in the range [1, n].

title: Minimum Cost to Merge Stones
description: There are n piles of stones arranged in a row. The ith pile has stones[i] stones. A move consists of merging exactly k consecutive piles into one pile, and the cost of this move is equal to the total number of stones in these k piles. Return the minimum cost to merge all piles of stones into one pile. If it is impossible, return -1.

title: Subarray With Elements Greater Than Varying Threshold
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer threshold. Find any subarray of nums of length k such that every element in the subarray is greater than threshold / k. Return the size of any such subarray. If no such subarray exists, return -1.

title: Max Sum of Rectangle No Larger Than K
description: Given an m x n matrix matrix and an integer k, return the max sum of a rectangle in the matrix such that its sum is no larger than k.

title: Sort Array by Moving Items to Empty Space
description: You are given an integer array nums of size n containing each element from 0 to n - 1 (0 represents empty space). In one operation, you can swap 0 with any adjacent or non-adjacent element. Return the minimum number of operations needed to sort nums in either ascending order (where 0 is at index 0 or index n - 1).
constraints: All the values of nums are unique.

title: Max Value of Equation
description: You are given an array points containing the coordinates of points on a 2D plane, sorted by the x-values, where points[i] = [xi, yi] such that xi < xj for all 1 <= i < j <= points.length. You are also given an integer k. Return the maximum value of the equation yi + yj + |xi - xj| where |xi - xj| <= k and 1 <= i < j <= points.length.
constraints: xi < xj for all 1 <= i < j <= points.length

title: Scramble String
description: We can scramble a string s to get a string t using recursive partition and swapping rules. Given two strings s1 and s2 of the same length, return true if s2 is a scrambled string of s1, otherwise return false.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Shortest Distance from All Buildings
description: You are given an m x n grid values of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 represents an empty land, 1 represents a building, and 2 represents an obstacle. You want to build a house on an empty land that reaches all buildings in the shortest total travel distance. Return the minimum distance, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: There will be at least one building in the grid.

title: All O`one Data Structure
description: Design a data structure to store the strings' count with the ability to return the strings with minimum and maximum counts in O(1) average time complexity. Implement the AllOne class supporting inc(key), dec(key), getMaxKey(), and getMinKey().
constraints: key consists of lowercase English letters.
It is guaranteed that for each call to dec, key exists in the data structure.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to inc, dec, getMaxKey, and getMinKey.

title: Tree of Coprimes
description: There is a tree consisting of n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1 and exactly n - 1 edges. Each node has a value. Return an array ans of size n where ans[i] is the closest ancestor to node i such that nums[i] and nums[ans[i]] are coprime, or -1 if no such ancestor exists.

title: Minimum Window Subsequence
description: Given strings s1 and s2, return the minimum contiguous substring part of s1, so that s2 is a subsequence of the part. If there is no such window in s1 that covers all characters in s2, return the empty string "". If there are multiple minimum-length windows, return the one that begins at the leftmost starting index.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Sum of Imbalance Numbers of All Subarrays
description: The imbalance number of a 0-indexed integer array arr of length n is defined as the number of indices in sarr (the sorted version of arr) where sarr[i+1] - sarr[i] > 1. Given an integer array nums, return the sum of imbalance numbers of all subarrays of nums.

title: Maximum Score from Performing Multiplication Operations
description: You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums and multipliers of size n and m respectively, where n >= m. You begin with a score of 0. In each step i from 0 to m - 1, you can choose one integer x from either the start or the end of nums, add multipliers[i] * x to your score, and remove x from nums. Return the maximum score after performing m operations.

title: Largest Component Size by Common Factor
description: You are given an integer array of unique positive integers nums. Consider the following graph: there are nums.length nodes, labeled nums[0] to nums[nums.length - 1]; there is an undirected edge between nums[i] and nums[j] if nums[i] and nums[j] share a common factor greater than 1. Return the size of the largest connected component in the graph.
constraints: All the values of nums are unique.

title: Read N Characters Given read4 II - Call Multiple Times
description: Given a file and assume that you can only read the file using a given method read4, implement a method read to read n characters. Your method read may be called multiple times.
constraints: file consists of English letters and digits.
At most 1000 calls will be made to read.

title: Rank Transform of a Matrix
description: Given an m x n matrix, return a new matrix answer where answer[row][col] is the rank of matrix[row][col]. The rank of an element is an integer that represents how large an element is compared to other elements in its row or column, such that rank is as small as possible while preserving relative orders.

title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps for K Consecutive Ones
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. nums comprises only 0's and 1's. In one move, you may choose two adjacent elements and swap them. Return the minimum number of adjacent swaps needed so that there are k consecutive 1's in the array.

title: Minimum Time to Remove All Cars Containing Illegal Goods
description: You are given a binary string s where s[i] = '1' represents that the ith train car contains illegal goods. You can remove train cars from either end (taking 1 unit of time per car) or from anywhere in the sequence (taking 2 units of time per car). Return the minimum time to remove all cars containing illegal goods.

title: Find in Mountain Array
description: Given a mountain array mountainArr, return the minimum index such that mountainArr.get(index) == target. If no such index exists, return -1. Accessing the mountain array must be done through MountainArray.get(k) and MountainArray.length(), with at most 100 calls allowed to get().

title: Recover the Original Array
description: Alice had a 0-indexed array arr of n positive integers and an integer k > 0. Two arrays lower and higher of length n were created where lower[i] = arr[i] - k and higher[i] = arr[i] + k. Both arrays were merged and shuffled into an array nums of size 2n. Given nums, recover and return any valid original array arr.
constraints: The input is generated such that at least one valid array arr exists.

title: Dungeon Game
description: The demons had captured the princess and imprisoned her in the bottom-right corner of a dungeon grid of size m x n. The knight starts in the top-left room and must reach the bottom-right room moving only right or down. Rooms have negative (demons) or positive (magic orbs) values. Return the knight's minimum initial health required so that his health never drops to 0 or below.

title: Fancy Sequence
description: Design an API for a sequence of numbers that supports appending an integer, adding an integer to all current elements, multiplying all current elements by an integer, and querying an element at a given index modulo 10^9 + 7.

examples.output: [null, null, null, null, null, 10, null, null, null, null, 26]

constraints: At most 10^5 calls total will be made to append, addAll, multAll, and getIndex.

title: Maximum Number of Groups Getting Fresh Donuts
description: There is a donuts shop that bakes donuts in batches of size batchSize. Customers arrive in groups. A group is happy if they receive donuts that are completely fresh from a newly opened batch. Return the maximum number of happy groups that can be achieved after rearranging the order of arrival of groups.

title: K-Similar Strings
description: Strings s1 and s2 are k-similar if we can swap the positions of two letters in s1 exactly k times so that the resulting string equals s2. Given two anagrams s1 and s2, return the smallest k for which s1 and s2 are k-similar.
constraints: s1 and s2 contain only lowercase letters from 'a' to 'f'.
s2 is an anagram of s1.

title: Distribute Repeating Integers
description: You are given an array of n integers nums and an array quantity of m integers, where quantity[i] is the number of integers the ith customer requires. Each customer requires all of their integers to be identical. Return true if you can satisfy all customer orders with the integers from nums, or false otherwise.

title: Minimum Unique Word Abbreviation
description: A string can be abbreviated by replacing any number of non-adjacent substrings with their lengths. Given a target string target and an array of strings dictionary, return an abbreviation of target of the shortest possible length such that it is not an abbreviation of any string in dictionary.
constraints: target and dictionary[i] consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Check if There Is a Valid Parentheses String Path
description: A parentheses string path in an m x n matrix grid of characters '(' and ')' is a path starting from (0, 0) and moving only down or right to (m - 1, n - 1). Return true if there exists at least one valid parentheses string path, or false otherwise.

title: Cat and Mouse II
description: A game is played by a cat and a mouse on an m x n grid. The mouse tries to reach the food while the cat tries to catch the mouse. Given catJump, mouseJump, and the grid layout with walls ('#'), mouse ('M'), cat ('C'), and food ('F'), return true if the mouse wins assuming both play optimally.

title: Maximum Score of a Node Sequence
description: There is an undirected graph with n nodes, numbered from 0 to n - 1. You are given a 0-indexed integer array scores of length n and a 2D integer array edges. A valid node sequence is a sequence of 4 distinct nodes connected by edges. Return the maximum score of a valid node sequence, or -1 if no such sequence exists.

title: Super Palindromes
description: A positive integer is a super-palindrome if it is a palindrome, and it is also the square of a palindrome. Given two positive integers left and right represented as strings, return the number of super-palindromes in the inclusive range [left, right].
constraints: left and right consist of only digits and do not contain leading zeros.

title: Rearrange String k Distance Apart
description: Given a string s and an integer k, rearrange s such that the same characters are at least distance k from each other. If it is not possible to rearrange the string, return an empty string "".
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Count of Range Sum
description: Given an integer array nums and two integers lower and upper, return the number of range sums that lie in [lower, upper] inclusive. The range sum S(i, j) is defined as the sum of the elements in nums between indices i and j inclusive.
constraints: The answer is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

title: Number of Digit One
description: Given an integer n, count the total number of digit 1 appearing in all non-negative integers less than or equal to n.

title: Minimum White Tiles After Covering With Carpets
description: You are given a 0-indexed binary string floor, where floor[i] = '1' represents a white tile and floor[i] = '0' represents a black tile. You are also given numCarpets and carpetLen. Return the minimum number of white tiles that are still visible after placing at most numCarpets carpets of length carpetLen.

title: Sliding Window Median
description: The median is the middle value in an ordered integer list. Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the median array for each window of size k moving from left to right across nums.

title: Kth Ancestor of a Tree Node
description: You are given a tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1 in the form of a parent array parent where parent[i] is the parent of ith node. The root of the tree is node 0. Implement the TreeAncestor class with getKthAncestor(node, k) returning the kth ancestor of the given node, or -1 if no such ancestor exists.
constraints: 0 <= parent[i] < n for all 0 < i < n
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to getKthAncestor.

title: Minimum Skips to Arrive at Meeting On Time
description: You are given an integer array dist, an integer speed, and an integer hoursBefore. After each segment, you must rest until the next integer hour, unless you choose to skip the rest. Return the minimum number of skips required to reach the destination within hoursBefore hours, or -1 if impossible.

title: Frog Position After T Seconds
description: Given an undirected tree with n vertices labeled from 1 to n. A frog starts at vertex 1 and in one second jumps with equal probability to any unvisited neighbor. When it has no unvisited neighbors, it stays on the same vertex. Return the probability that after t seconds the frog is on the vertex target.

title: Perfect Rectangle
description: Given an array rectangles where rectangles[i] = [xi, yi, ai, bi] represents an axis-aligned rectangle from bottom-left (xi, yi) to top-right (ai, bi), return true if all rectangles together form an exact rectangular cover without overlapping or leaving empty space.

title: K Empty Slots
description: You have n bulbs labeled from 1 to n in a row. You are given an integer array bulbs of size n where bulbs[i] = x indicates that on day i + 1, the bulb at position x is turned on. Return the earliest day on which there exist two turned-on bulbs with exactly k turned-off bulbs between them, or -1 if no such day exists.
constraints: bulbs is a permutation of numbers from 1 to n.

title: Maximum Average Subarray II
description: You are given an integer array nums consisting of n integers, and an integer k. Find a contiguous subarray whose length is greater than or equal to k that has the maximum average value, and return this value. Any answer with a calculation error less than 10^-5 will be accepted.

title: Bricks Falling When Hit
description: You are given an m x n binary grid, where each 1 represents a brick and 0 represents an empty space. A brick is stable if it is directly connected to the top of the grid or at least one of its four neighbors is stable. You are also given an array hits. Erasing bricks causes unstable bricks to fall. Return an array result where each result[i] is the number of bricks that fall after the ith hit.

title: Palindrome Partitioning II
description: Given a string s, partition s such that every substring of the partition is a palindrome. Return the minimum cuts needed for a palindrome partitioning of s.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only.

title: Palindrome Pairs
description: Given a 0-indexed array of unique strings words, return all the pairs of integers (i, j) such that i != j and the concatenation of the two strings words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Redundant Connection II
description: In this problem, a rooted tree is a directed graph such that there is exactly one node (the root) for which all other nodes are descendants of this node, and every node has exactly one parent, except for the root. Given a directed graph with n nodes and n directed edges where each node is labeled from 1 to n, return an edge that can be removed so that the resulting graph is a rooted tree of n nodes. If there are multiple answers, return the one that occurs last in the given 2D-array.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Eat N Oranges
description: There are n oranges in the kitchen and you decided to eat some oranges each day as follows: eat one orange, eat 2*(n/3) oranges if n is divisible by 3, or eat n/2 oranges if n is divisible by 2. Return the minimum number of days to eat all n oranges.

title: Create Maximum Number
description: You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths m and n respectively and an integer k.
