Create the maximum number of length k <= m + n from digits of the two numbers while preserving the relative order of the digits from the same array. Return an array of the k digits representing the answer.

title: Maximum Number of Ways to Partition an Array
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n. A pivot index p (0 <= p < n - 1) is valid if the sum of elements from 0 to p equals the sum of elements from p + 1 to n - 1. You can change at most one element of nums to any integer k. Return the maximum possible number of pivot indices in the array after the change.

title: Cat and Mouse
description: A game on an undirected graph is played by a mouse starting at node 1 and a cat starting at node 2. Node 0 is the hole. In each turn, mouse and cat take turns moving to adjacent nodes. Mouse wins if it reaches node 0, Cat wins if it catches the mouse, or Draw (0) if positions repeat. Return 1 if mouse wins, 2 if cat wins, or 0 if draw, assuming both play optimally.

title: Random Pick with Blacklist
description: You are given an integer n and an array of unique integers blacklist. Design an algorithm to pick a random integer in the range [0, n - 1] that is not in blacklist. Any integer not in blacklist should be equally likely to be returned. Implement the Solution class.
constraints: All the values of blacklist are unique.
At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made to pick.

title: String Transforms Into Another String
description: Given two strings str1 and str2 of the same length, return true if and only if you can convert str1 into str2 by doing zero or more conversions, where in one conversion you can convert all occurrences of one character in str1 to any other lowercase English character.
constraints: str1 and str2 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Reaching Points
description: Given four integers sx, sy, tx, and ty, return true if it is possible to convert the point (sx, sy) to the point (tx, ty) through some operations, or false otherwise. A move consists of transforming the point (x, y) to either (x, x + y) or (x + y, y).

title: Coin Path
description: You are given an integer array coins (1-indexed) of size n and an integer maxJump. In each step, you can jump from index i to index i + k where 1 <= k <= maxJump. Landing on index j costs coins[j] coins (if coins[j] == -1, the index cannot be visited). Return the path of indices that achieves the minimum cost from index 1 to index n. If there are multiple paths with the same minimum cost, return the lexicographically smallest path, or an empty array if unreachable.

title: Maximize Consecutive Elements in an Array After Modification
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums. You can increase the value of any element by at most 1, at most once per element. Return the maximum possible length of a consecutive sequence of integers that can be formed from the elements of nums after modifications.

title: Longest Balanced Subarray II
description: You are given an integer array nums. A subarray is called balanced if the frequency of every unique element within the subarray satisfies specific balance constraints. Return the length of the longest balanced subarray.

title: Number of Beautiful Partitions
description: You are given a string s that consists of the digits '1' to '9' and two integers k and minLength. A partition of s into k non-empty substrings is called beautiful if the first character of each substring is a prime digit ('2', '3', '5', or '7'), the last character is a non-prime digit, and the length of each substring is at least minLength. Return the number of beautiful partitions of s modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s consists of the digits '1' to '9'.

title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the length of the shortest non-empty subarray of nums with a sum of at least k. If there is no such subarray, return -1.

title: Longest Duplicate Substring
description: Given a string s, consider all duplicated substrings: substrings of s that occur 2 or more times. The occurrences may overlap. Return any duplicated substring that has the longest possible length. If s does not have a duplicated substring, the answer is "".
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Sum of Good Subsequences
description: Given an integer array nums, a subsequence is called good if the absolute difference between any two adjacent elements in the subsequence is exactly 1. Return the sum of all good subsequences modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Parallel Courses II
description: You are given an integer n, which indicates that there are n courses labeled from 1 to n. You are also given an array relations where relations[i] = [prevCoursei, nextCoursei] and an integer k. In one semester, you can take at most k courses as long as you have taken all the prerequisites. Return the minimum number of semesters needed to take all courses.

title: Max Points on a Line
description: Given an array of points where points[i] = [xi, yi] represents a point on the X-Y plane, return the maximum number of points that lie on the same straight line.

title: Super Egg Drop
description: You are given k identical eggs and you have access to a building with n floors labeled from 1 to n. There exists a floor f (0 <= f <= n) such that any egg dropped from a floor higher than f will break, and any egg dropped from or below floor f will not break. Return the minimum number of moves that you need to determine with certainty what the value of f is.

title: Count K-Subsequences of a String With Maximum Beauty
description: You are given a string s and an integer k. A k-subsequence is a subsequence of length k consisting of unique characters from s. The beauty of a k-subsequence is defined as the sum of frequencies of its characters in s. Return the number of k-subsequences with the maximum beauty modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array II
description: You are given a 0-indexed string s, string a, string b, and an integer k. An index i is beautiful if 0 <= i <= s.length - a.length, s[i..(i + a.length - 1)] == a, and there exists an index j such that 0 <= j <= s.length - b.length, s[j..(j + b.length - 1)] == b, and |j - i| <= k. Return the array of all beautiful indices in ascending order.
constraints: s, a, and b contain only lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Sum of Values by Dividing Array
description: You are given two arrays of integers nums and andValues of length n and m respectively. You must divide nums into m non-empty contiguous subarrays such that the bitwise AND of elements in the ith subarray equals andValues[i]. The value of a subarray is its last element. Return the minimum possible sum of values of the m subarrays, or -1 if no valid division exists.

title: Word Ladder II
description: A transformation sequence from word beginWord to word endWord using a dictionary wordList is a sequence of words beginWord -> s1 -> s2 -> ... -> sk such that every adjacent pair of words differs by a single letter, and every si is in wordList. Given two words, beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, return all the shortest transformation sequences from beginWord to endWord, or an empty list if no such sequence exists.
constraints: beginWord, endWord, and wordList[i] consist of lowercase English letters.
All the words in wordList are unique.

title: String Transformation
description: You are given two strings s and t of equal length n. You can perform an operation on s where you choose an integer l (1 <= l < n) and move the suffix of s of length l to the front. Return the number of ways to transform s into t in exactly k operations modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence II
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. Find the length of the longest subsequence of nums that meets the following conditions: the subsequence is strictly increasing, and the difference between adjacent elements in the subsequence is at most k.

title: Maximize Subarray GCD Score
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer k. You can perform at most k operations where in each operation you can choose any element and multiply it by 2. Return the maximum possible score of a subarray, where score is defined as the length of the subarray multiplied by the greatest common divisor (GCD) of its elements.

title: Count Non-Decreasing Subarrays After K Operations
description: You are given an array nums of integers and an integer k. In one operation, you can increase any element nums[i] by 1. A subarray is valid if we can make it non-decreasing using at most k total increments across the elements in the subarray. Return the number of non-empty valid subarrays of nums.

title: Find the Maximum Sequence Value of Array
description: You are given an integer array nums and a positive integer k. An integer is called the sequence value of an array of length 2k if it can be represented as the bitwise XOR of the bitwise OR of the first k elements and the bitwise OR of the last k elements. Return the maximum possible sequence value among all subsequences of length 2k from nums.

title: Check if DFS Strings Are Palindromes
description: You are given a tree rooted at node 0 with n nodes, a string s of length n where s[i] represents the character at node i, and a parent array parent. A DFS string for a node is formed by concatenating characters visited in its subtree in pre-order traversal. Return a boolean array answer of size n where answer[i] is true if the DFS string of the subtree rooted at node i is a palindrome.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Booking Concert Tickets in Groups
description: A concert hall has n rows numbered from 0 to n - 1, each with m seats numbered from 0 to m - 1. Implement the BookMyShow class that supports gather(k, maxRow) (books k consecutive seats in the smallest available row <= maxRow) and scatter(k, maxRow) (books k seats across any available seats in rows <= maxRow).
constraints: At most 5 * 10^4 calls total will be made to gather and scatter.

title: Recover a Tree From Preorder Traversal
description: We run a preorder depth-first search on the root of a binary tree. At each node in this traversal, we output D dashes (where D is the depth of this node), then we output the value of this node. Given the output traversal string, recover the binary tree and return its root.
constraints: The number of nodes in the original tree is in the range [1, 1000].

title: Maximum Score Words Formed by Letters
description: Given a list of words, a list of single letters (which might be repeating) and the score of every character. Return the maximum score of any valid set of words formed by using the given letters (words[i] cannot be used more than once, each letter can only be used as many times as it appears).
constraints: words[i], letters[i] contain only lowercase English letters.

title: Number of Ways to Paint N Ã— 3 Grid
description: You have a grid of size n x 3 and you want to paint each cell of the grid with exactly one of the three colors: Red, Yellow, or Green while making sure that no two adjacent cells have the same color. Return the number of ways you can paint this grid modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Special Binary String
description: Special binary strings are binary strings that have equal numbers of 0's and 1's, and every prefix has at least as many 1's as 0's. Given a special string s, a move consists of choosing two consecutive non-empty special substrings of s and swapping them. Return the lexicographically largest resulting string possible after any number of moves.
constraints: s is a special binary string.

title: Minimum One Bit Operations to Make Integers Zero
description: Given an integer n, you must transform it into 0 using operations: change the 0th bit, or change the ith bit if the (i-1)th bit is 1 and all bits from (i-2) to 0 are 0. Return the minimum number of operations to transform n into 0.

title: Delete Duplicate Folders in System
description: Due to a bug, there are many duplicate folders in a file system. Two folders are identical if they have the same subfolder structure. Delete all duplicate subtrees and return the 2D array of remaining folder paths in any order.
constraints: paths[i][j] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Reducing Dishes
description: A chef has collected data on the satisfaction level of his n dishes. Chef can cook any dish in 1 unit of time. Like-time coefficient of a dish is defined as the time taken to cook that dish including previous dishes multiplied by its satisfaction level. Return the maximum sum of like-time coefficient that the chef can obtain after dishes preparation.

title: Minimum Initial Energy to Finish Tasks
description: You are given an array tasks where tasks[i] = [actuali, minimumi]. To start task i you need at least minimumi energy, and finishing it consumes actuali energy. Return the minimum initial energy required to finish all tasks.

title: Minimum Score After Removals on a Tree
description: There is an undirected connected tree with n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1 and n - 1 edges. You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a 2D integer array edges. An operation consists of removing two distinct edges to create three connected components. The score of this removal is the difference between the largest and smallest component XOR values. Return the minimum score among all valid pairs of edge removals.

title: Jump Game V
description: Given an array of integers arr and an integer d. In one step you can jump from index i to index i + x or i - x where 0 < x <= d such that arr[i] > arr[j] for all indices j between i and the destination. Return the maximum number of indices you can visit.

title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
description: Given a matrix and a target, return the number of non-empty submatrices that sum to target.

title: Sliding Puzzle
description: On a 2 x 3 board, there are five tiles labeled from 1 to 5, and an empty square represented by 0. A move consists of choosing 0 and a 4-directionally adjacent number and swapping it. Return the least number of moves required so that the state of the board is solved ([[1,2,3],[4,5,0]]), or -1 if impossible.
constraints: Each value from 0 to 5 appears exactly once.

title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make a String Palindrome
description: Given a string s. In one step you can insert any character at any position of the string. Return the minimum number of steps to make s a palindrome.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Maximize the Number of Target Nodes After Connecting Trees II
description: There exist two undirected trees with n and m nodes. A target node from node u is a node at an even distance from u. You can add an edge connecting one node in tree1 to one node in tree2. Return an array answer of size n where answer[i] is the maximum possible number of target nodes for node i in tree1 after connecting the two trees.

title: Number of Ways to Assign Edge Weights II
description: You are given an undirected graph with n nodes and an array edges. You must assign positive integer weights to unweighted edges such that shortest path distances between query pairs satisfy given constraints. Return the number of valid weight assignments modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Put Marbles in Bags
description: You have k bags and n marbles of weights weights[i]. Distribute weights into k contiguous sub-arrays. The score is the sum of endpoints of each bag. Return the difference between the maximum and minimum score among all distributions.

title: Longest Subsequence Repeated k Times
description: You are given a string s of length n, and an integer k. You are tasked to find the longest subsequence repeated k times in string s. If multiple such subsequences exist, return the lexicographically largest one.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable
description: Alice and Bob have an undirected graph of n nodes and 3 types of edges: Type 1 (Alice can traverse), Type 2 (Bob can traverse), Type 3 (both can traverse). Return the maximum number of edges you can remove such that the graph remains fully traversable for both, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: All tuples (typei, ui, vi) are distinct.

title: Minimum Difference in Sums After Removal of Elements
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums consisting of 3 * n elements. You are allowed to remove any n elements from nums. The difference of sums of the remaining 2 * n elements is defined as (sum of first n elements) - (sum of last n elements). Return the minimum difference possible after removing n elements.

title: Max Dot Product of Two Subsequences
description: Given two arrays nums1 and nums2. Return the maximum dot product between non-empty subsequences of nums1 and nums2 with the same length.

title: Find the Maximum Sum of Node Values
description: There exists an undirected tree with n nodes numbered 0 to n - 1. You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array edges and a 0-indexed array nums of length n. You can choose any edge (u, v) and simultaneously update nums[u] = nums[u] XOR k and nums[v] = nums[v] XOR k. Return the maximum possible sum of elements of nums after performing any number of operations.

title: Count Subarrays With Fixed Bounds
description: You are given an integer array nums and two integers minK and maxK. A fixed-bound subarray of nums is a subarray that satisfies the following conditions: the minimum value in the subarray is equal to minK, and the maximum value in the subarray is equal to maxK. Return the number of fixed-bound subarrays.

title: Find the Count of Good Integers
description: You are given two positive integers n and k. An n-digit integer is called good if its digits can be rearranged to form a palindrome of length n that is divisible by k without leading zeros. Return the count of good integers of length n.

title: Serialize and Deserialize N-ary Tree
description: Serialization is the process of converting a data structure or object into a sequence of bits so that it can be stored in a file or memory buffer, or transmitted across a network connection link to be reconstructed later in the same or another computer environment. Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize an N-ary tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
The height of the n-ary tree is less than or equal to 1000.

title: Minimum Cost Walk in Weighted Graph
description: There is an undirected weighted graph with n vertices. You are given an array edges and an array query where query[i] = [si, ti]. The cost of a walk is the bitwise AND of weights of all edges traversed. Return an array ans where ans[i] is the minimum cost of a walk from si to ti, or -1 if no walk exists.

title: Number of ZigZag Arrays II
description: Given integers n, l, and r, return the number of distinct arrays of length n with elements in the range [l, r] that satisfy zigzag monotonicity constraints modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximum Candies You Can Get from Boxes
description: You have n boxes labeled from 0 to n - 1. You are given arrays status, candies, keys, containedBoxes, and initialBoxes. Return the maximum number of candies you can collect by opening accessible and unlocked boxes.

title: Maximum Building Height
description: You want to build n buildings numbered from 1 to n. The height of building 1 must be 0, and the absolute height difference between adjacent buildings is at most 1. You are given a 2D integer array restrictions where restrictions[j] = [idj, maxHeightj]. Return the maximum possible height of the tallest building.

title: Maximum Frequency Stack
description: Design a stack-like data structure to push elements to the stack and pop the most frequent element from the stack. Implement the FreqStack class supporting push(val) and pop(). If there is a tie for the most frequent element, the element closest to the top of the stack is removed and returned.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made to push and pop.

title: Divide Nodes Into the Maximum Number of Groups
description: You are given a positive integer n representing the number of nodes in an undirected graph, and a 2D integer array edges. Divide the nodes into m groups such that each edge connects nodes in adjacent groups (|group[u] - group[v]| = 1). Return the maximum number of groups m, or -1 if no valid grouping exists.

title: Chalkboard XOR Game
description: An array of integers nums is written on a chalkboard. Alice and Bob take turns erasing numbers. A player loses if erasing an element makes the bitwise XOR sum of all remaining elements equal to 0. If the XOR sum is already 0 at the start of a player's turn, that player wins immediately. Assuming optimal play, return true if Alice wins, or false otherwise.

title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
description: Given a weighted undirected connected graph with n vertices numbered from 0 to n - 1, and an array edges, find all the critical and pseudo-critical edges in the minimum spanning tree (MST) of the graph.

title: Valid Arrangement of Pairs
description: You are given a 2D integer array pairs where pairs[i] = [starti, endi]. An arrangement of pairs is valid if endi-1 == starti for all 1 <= i < pairs.length. Return any valid arrangement of pairs.

title: Maximize Spanning Tree Stability with Upgrades
description: You are given a connected weighted graph with n vertices and edges. You are also given an integer budget. You can spend budget to upgrade edge capacities. Return the maximum stability achievable for a spanning tree.

title: Sort Items by Groups Respecting Dependencies
description: There are n items each belonging to zero or one group, and a list of dependencies between items. Sort all items such that items of the same group appear consecutively and all item-level and group-level dependencies are satisfied. Return the sorted list, or empty array if impossible.

title: Check If It Is a Good Array
description: Given an array nums of positive integers. Your goal is to select a subset of nums, multiply each element by an integer and add them up, such that the sum equals 1. Return true if such subset exists, otherwise return false.

title: Build Array Where You Can Find The Maximum Exactly K Comparisons
description: You are given three integers n, m, and k. Consider the search cost algorithm for finding maximum. Build an array of length n where 1 <= arr[i] <= m such that search cost is exactly k. Return the number of such arrays modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Make Array Non-decreasing or Non-increasing
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums. In one operation, you can choose any element and increase or decrease it by 1. Return the minimum number of operations to make nums non-decreasing or non-increasing.

title: Count Good Triplets in an Array
description: You are given two 0-indexed arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n, both of which are permutations of [0, 1, ..., n - 1]. A good triplet is a set of 3 distinct values that occur in increasing order of indices in both arrays. Return the total number of good triplets.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 are permutations of [0, n - 1].

title: Find the Maximum Number of Fruits Collected
description: There is an n x n grid where fruits[i][j] represents the number of fruits in that cell. Three children start at (0, 0), (0, n - 1), and (n - 1, 0) and move towards (n - 1, n - 1) according to specific movement rules. Return the maximum total fruits collected by all three children.

title: Count All Valid Pickup and Delivery Options
description: Given n orders, each order consist in pickup and delivery services. Count all valid pickup/delivery sequences such that delivery(i) is always after pickup(i). Return the answer modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximize Alternating Sum Using Swaps
description: You are given an integer array nums and a list of pairs of indices that can be swapped. Return the maximum alternating sum achievable after any number of valid swaps.

title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph II
description: You are given an undirected graph with n nodes labeled 0 to n - 1 and an array edges with weights. You are also given an array nums where nums[i] represents the value of node i, and queries where queries[j] = [uj, vj, limitj]. Return a boolean array answer where answer[j] is true if there exists a valid path between uj and vj such that every edge on the path has a weight at most limitj and the path satisfies the node parity conditions, or false otherwise.

title: Maximize Subarrays After Removing One Conflicting Pair
description: You are given an integer n and a 2D integer array conflictingPairs of length m. A subarray [l, r] (1 <= l <= r <= n) is valid if no pair (a, b) in conflictingPairs has both a and b in [l, r]. You can remove at most one conflicting pair from conflictingPairs. Return the maximum possible number of valid subarrays.

title: Number of Paths with Max Score
description: You are given a square board of characters. You can move on the board starting at the bottom right square 'S' to the top left square 'E' moving only up, left, or up-left. Return an array [max_score, num_paths] modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: board[i][j] is 'E', 'S', 'X', or a digit from '0' to '9'.

title: Maximum Score From Grid Operations
description: You are given an n x n matrix grid of positive integers. For each column, you can choose to color the first k cells black. If a white cell has a horizontally adjacent black cell, its value is added to the total score. Return the maximum score achievable.

title: Sum of k-Mirror Numbers
description: A k-mirror number is a positive integer with no leading zeros that is a palindrome in base-10 and base-k. Given integers k and n, return the sum of the n smallest k-mirror numbers.

title: Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones II
description: You are given a 2D binary array grid. Find the minimum possible total area of 3 non-overlapping axis-aligned rectangles that collectively cover all the 1's in the grid.
constraints: The total number of 1's in grid is at least 3.

title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended II
description: You are given an array of events where events[i] = [startDayi, endDayi, valuei] and an integer k. You can attend at most k non-overlapping events. Return the maximum sum of values that you can receive by attending events.

title: Minimum Total Distance Traveled
description: There are some robots and factories on the X-axis. You are given an integer array robot and a 2D integer array factory where factory[j] = [positionj, limitj]. Return the minimum total distance traveled by all robots so that every robot is repaired by a factory.
constraints: The input will be generated such that it is always possible to repair every robot.

title: Find the String with LCP
description: We define the lcp matrix of any string word of length n where lcp[i][j] is the length of the longest common prefix between substrings starting at index i and index j. Given an n x n matrix lcp, return the lexicographically smallest lowercase English string word that corresponds to lcp, or an empty string "" if no such string exists.

title: Maximum Path Quality of a Graph
description: There is an undirected graph with n nodes (0 to n - 1) and values values[i]. You start at node 0 and have maxTime time. Return the maximum quality of a valid path starting and ending at node 0 within maxTime, where quality is the sum of unique visited node values.

title: Closest Node to Path in Tree
description: You are given an undirected tree with n nodes and an array query where query[i] = [starti, endi, nodei]. Return an array ans where ans[i] is the node on the simple path between starti and endi that is closest to nodei.

title: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
description: You are given a binary array nums and an integer k. A k-bit flip involves choosing a contiguous subarray of length k and simultaneously changing every 0 to 1 and every 1 to 0. Return the minimum number of k-bit flips required so that there is no 0 in the array, or -1 if impossible.

title: Second Minimum Time to Reach Destination
description: A city is represented by an undirected graph of n vertices (1 to n). All edges take time time to traverse. Traffic lights at each vertex switch between green and red every change minutes. Return the second minimum time to reach vertex n from vertex 1.

title: Maximum Height by Stacking Cuboids
description: Given n cuboids where dimensions of the ith cuboid are cuboids[i] = [widthi, lengthi, heighti]. You can rotate cuboids and place one on top of another if width, length, and height are all <= the one below it. Return the maximum height of the stacked cuboids.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make Array Divisible
description: You are given two positive integer arrays nums and numsDivide. You can delete any number of elements from nums. Return the minimum number of deletions such that the smallest element in nums divides all elements of numsDivide, or -1 if impossible.

title: Robot Collisions
description: There are n 1-indexed robots with given positions, healths, and directions ('L' or 'R'). They move simultaneously at equal speed. When two robots collide, the one with lower health is removed and the survivor loses 1 health (or both removed if equal). Return the health of surviving robots in the original order.
constraints: All values in positions are distinct.

title: Best Meeting Point
description: Given an m x n binary grid grid where each 1 marks the home of one friend, return the minimal total travel distance using Manhattan distance for all friends to meet at a single point.
constraints: There will be at least two friends in the grid.

title: Maximize the Minimum Powered City
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array stations of length n, where stations[i] represents the number of power stations in the ith city. Each power station provides power to cities within distance r. You can build up to k additional power stations. Return the maximum possible minimum power of any city.

title: Paint House III
description: There is a row of m houses, some already painted and some not (houses[i] == 0). You have n colors and cost[i][j] to paint house i with color j + 1. A neighborhood is a maximal group of continuous houses of the same color. Paint unpainted houses such that there are exactly target neighborhoods with minimum total cost. Return minimum cost, or -1 if impossible.

title: Department Top Three Salaries
description: A company's executives are interested in seeing who earns the most money in each of the company's departments. A high earner in a department is an employee who has a salary in the top three unique salaries for that department. Write a solution to find the employees who are high earners in each of the departments.
constraints: id is the primary key column for Employee.
departmentId is a foreign key of the ID from Department.

title: Strange Printer
description: There is a strange printer with two special requirements: the printer can only print a sequence of the same character each time, and at each turn, the printer can print new characters over existing characters. Given a string s, return the minimum number of turns the printer needed to print it.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Maximum Fruits Harvested After at Most K Steps
description: Fruits are placed at various positions on an infinite number line. You are given a 2D integer array fruits where fruits[i] = [positioni, amounti] and integers startPos and k. Starting at startPos, you can walk at most k steps. Return the maximum total number of fruits you can harvest.

title: Data Stream as Disjoint Intervals
description: Given a data stream input of non-negative integers a1, a2, ..., an, summarize the numbers seen so far as a list of disjoint intervals. Implement the SummaryRanges class supporting addNum(value) and getIntervals().
constraints: At most 3 * 10^4 calls will be made to addNum and getIntervals.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Elements Zero
description: You are given an integer array nums. In one operation, you can choose a contiguous subarray and decrement all its positive elements by 1. Return the minimum number of operations to make all elements of nums equal to 0.

title: Minimum Edge Reversals So Every Node Is Reachable
description: There is a directed tree with n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1 with n - 1 edges. Return an array answer of size n where answer[i] is the minimum number of edge reversals needed so that every other node is reachable from node i.

title: Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule
description: You want to schedule a list of jobs in d days. Jobs are dependent (i.e To work on the ith job, you have to finish all the jobs j where 0 <= j < i). You have to finish at least one task every day. The difficulty of a day is the maximum difficulty of a job done in that day. Return the minimum difficulty of a job schedule. If you cannot find a schedule for the jobs return -1.

title: Minimum Cost to Convert String II
description: You are given two 0-indexed strings source and target, both of length n and consisting of lowercase English characters. You are also given two 0-indexed string arrays original and changed, and an integer array cost, where cost[i] represents the cost of converting the string original[i] to the string changed[i]. In one operation, you can pick a substring x from source and replace it with y if there exists an index i such that original[i] == x and changed[i] == y. Return the minimum cost to convert source to target, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: source, target consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Maximum Number of Points From Grid Queries
description: You are given an m x n integer matrix grid and an array queries of size k. For each query queries[i], you start at (0, 0) and can move to any 4-directionally adjacent cell if its value is strictly less than queries[i]. Return an array ans of size k where ans[i] is the maximum number of points you can get for queries[i].

title: Poor Pigs
description: There are buckets of liquid, where exactly one bucket is poisonous. To figure out which bucket is poisonous, you feed some pigs simultaneously and wait for a minutesToDie duration before running the next round of tests. Given buckets, minutesToDie, and minutesToTest, return the minimum number of pigs needed to determine the poisonous bucket within minutesToTest minutes.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Disconnect Island
description: You are given an m x n binary grid grid where 1 represents land and 0 represents water. An island is a maximal 4-directionally connected group of 1s. The grid is disconnected if it has 0 islands or more than 1 island. In one day, you can change any land cell (1) into water (0). Return the minimum number of days to disconnect the grid.

title: Count the Number of Arrays with K Matching Adjacent Elements
description: You are given three positive integers n, m, and k. Return the number of integer arrays arr of length n such that each element is between 1 and m (inclusive), and there are exactly k indices i (1 <= i < n) such that arr[i] == arr[i - 1]. Return the answer modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Set Intersection Size At Least Two
description: You are given a 2D integer array intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi]. An integer interval is containing a set S if S contains at least two distinct integers from [starti, endi] for all i. Return the minimum possible size of a containing set S.

title: Total Characters in String After Transformations II
description: You are given a string s, an integer t, and an integer array nums of length 26. In one transformation, each character c in s is replaced by the next nums[c - 'a'] characters in the alphabet (wrapping around from 'z' to 'a'). Return the total length of the string after t transformations modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Replace Non-Coprime Numbers in Array
description: You are given an array of integers nums. Perform the following steps: find two adjacent numbers in nums that are non-coprime (GCD > 1), replace them with their LCM, and repeat until no adjacent non-coprime numbers exist. Return the final modified array.
constraints: The input is generated such that the final numbers will fit in a 32-bit integer.

title: Rearranging Fruits
description: You have two fruit baskets containing n fruits each. You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays basket1 and basket2 representing the cost of fruits in each basket. You can swap any fruit from basket1 with any fruit from basket2 with cost min(basket1[i], basket2[j]). Return the minimum total cost to make both baskets have identical fruit collections, or -1 if impossible.

title: Find Minimum Diameter After Merging Two Trees
description: There exist two undirected trees with n and m nodes. You must connect one node from the first tree to one node in the second tree with an edge. Return the minimum possible diameter of the resulting merged tree.

title: Count the Number of Ideal Arrays
description: You are given two integers n and maxValue. An array arr of length n is called ideal if every element is between 1 and maxValue (inclusive), and for each 1 <= i < n, arr[i] is divisible by arr[i - 1]. Return the number of distinct ideal arrays of length n modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Allocate Mailboxes
description: Given the array houses where houses[i] is the location of the ith house along a street, and an integer k, allocate k mailboxes along the street such that the total distance between each house and its nearest mailbox is minimized. Return the minimum total distance.
constraints: All integers in houses are distinct.

title: Total Waviness of Numbers in Range II
description: The waviness of a number is defined as the number of peak and valley digits in its decimal representation. Given two integers low and high, return the total sum of waviness across all numbers in the inclusive range [low, high] modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Total Appeal of A String
description: The appeal of a string is the number of distinct characters found in the string. Given a string s, return the total appeal of all of its substrings.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Constrained Subsequence Sum
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the maximum sum of a non-empty subsequence of that array such that for every two consecutive integers in the subsequence, nums[i] and nums[j], where i < j, the condition j - i <= k is satisfied.

title: Maximum Profit from Trading Stocks with Discounts
description: You are given arrays present, future, and discount, along with an initial budget. For each stock, you can buy at present price or discounted price if applicable and sell at future price. Return the maximum profit achievable within budget.

title: Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary
description: You are given a list of strings of the same length words and a string target. Your task is to form target using the given words. To form the ith character of target, you can choose the kth character of any string in words as long as k > index of previous chosen character. Return the number of ways to form target modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: All strings in words have the same length.
words[i] and target consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
description: You have n computers. You are given the integer n and an integer array batteries where the ith battery can run a computer for batteries[i] minutes. You want to run all n computers simultaneously. At any point you can insert any battery into any computer. Return the maximum number of minutes you can run all n computers simultaneously.

title: Rectangle Area II
description: You are given a 2D array of axis-aligned rectangles. Each rectangle[i] = [xi1, yi1, xi2, yi2] denotes the bottom-left and top-right coordinates. Calculate the total area covered by all rectangles in the plane. Any area covered by two or more rectangles should only be counted once. Return the total area modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Length of Longest V-Shaped Diagonal Segment
description: You are given an m x n 2D integer matrix grid. A V-shaped diagonal segment starts at a cell with value 1, moves diagonally in a direction, makes at most one 90-degree clockwise turn, and alternates between values 2 and 0 (1 -> 2 -> 0 -> 2 -> 0...). Return the length of the longest valid V-shaped diagonal segment.

title: Minimum Time to Visit a Cell In a Grid
description: You are given an m x n matrix grid of non-negative integers where grid[row][col] represents the minimum time required to visit that cell. You start at (0, 0) at time t = 0. In each step, you can move to any 4-adjacent cell in 1 unit of time, but can only enter if current time + 1 >= grid[row][col]. Return the minimum time to reach (m - 1, n - 1), or -1 if unreachable.

title: Modify Graph Edge Weights
description: You are given an undirected weighted connected graph having n nodes, an array edges where edges[i] = [ai, bi, wi] (with wi = -1 denoting modifiable edges), and integers source, destination, and target. Modify all modifiable edges such that the shortest path between source and destination is exactly target. Return the modified edges, or an empty array if impossible.

title: Number of Distinct Islands II
description: You are given an m x n binary matrix grid. An island is considered the same as another if and only if one island can be translated, rotated (90, 180, or 270 degrees), or reflected to match the other. Return the number of distinct islands.

title: Minimum Cost for Cutting Cake II
description: There is an m x n cake that needs to be cut into 1 x 1 pieces. You are given integers m, n, and two 1D arrays horizontalCut and verticalCut where horizontalCut[i] is the cost of cutting horizontally along line i and verticalCut[j] is the cost of cutting vertically along line j. Each cut cuts all cake pieces along that line. Return the minimum total cost to cut the cake into 1 x 1 pieces.

title: Arithmetic Slices II - Subsequence
description: Given an integer array nums, return the number of all the arithmetic subsequences of nums. A sequence of numbers is called arithmetic if it consists of at least three elements and if the difference between any two consecutive elements is the same.

title: Contain Virus
description: A virus is spreading on an m x n grid. Infected cells are 1, uninfected cells are 0, and installed walls are 2. Each day, the virus threatens uninfected neighbors. You can build walls around the infected region that threatens the most uninfected cells to contain it, while other regions spread. Return the number of walls used to contain all virus spread.

title: Minimum Number of Removals to Make Mountain Array
description: An array arr is a mountain array if and only if arr.length >= 3 and there exists some index i (0 < i < arr.length - 1) such that arr[0] < arr[1] < ... < arr[i] and arr[i] > arr[i + 1] > ... > arr[arr.length - 1]. Given an integer array nums, return the minimum number of elements to remove to make nums a mountain array.

title: Divide an Array Into Subarrays With Minimum Cost II
description: You are given a 0-indexed array of integers nums of length n, and two positive integers k and dist. The cost of an array is the value of its first element. You need to divide nums into k contiguous subarrays such that the difference between the starting index of the second subarray and the starting index of the kth subarray is at most dist. Return the minimum possible sum of the cost of these subarrays.

title: Smallest Rotation with Highest Score
description: You are given an integer array nums. A rotation of nums by k means shift all elements to the left by k places. A point is scored for every index i where nums[i] <= i. Return the rotation index k that corresponds to the highest possible score. If there are multiple answers, return the smallest such index k.

title: Maximum Students Taking Exam
description: Given a m x n matrix seats that represents a classroom, where seats[i][j] == '#' means a broken seat and seats[i][j] == '.' means a good seat. Students cannot sit in broken seats, nor can they sit next to each other horizontally, or diagonally in front (upper left and upper right). Return the maximum number of students that can take the exam simultaneously.

title: Parse Lisp Expression
description: You are given a string expression representing a Lisp-like expression to return the integer value of it. The valid expressions are integers, let expressions (variable assignments), add expressions, and mult expressions.

examples.input: expression = "(let x 2 (mult x (let x 3 y 4 (add x y))))"
expression = "(let x 1 y 2 x (add x y) (add x y))"

constraints: There are no leading or trailing spaces in expression.
All tokens are separated by a single space in expression.
The given expression is always verified to be valid and evaluate to a single integer.

title: IPO
description: Suppose LeetCode will start its IPO soon. In order to sell a good price of its shares, LeetCode wants to finish some projects to increase its capital before the IPO. Given integers k, w, and arrays profits and capital, return the maximum capital you can have after finishing at most k distinct projects.

title: Apply Operations to Maximize Score
description: You are given an array nums of n positive integers and an integer k. The prime score of an integer is the number of distinct prime factors it has. You choose a non-empty subarray, find the element with highest prime score (or first occurrence if tied), and multiply your total score by that element. You can do this operation at most k times. Return the maximum score modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Generated String
description: You are given two strings str1 and str2 of lengths n and m respectively. A string word of length n + m - 1 is generated such that for each index i from 0 to n - 1, if str1[i] == 'T', the substring of word of length m starting at i equals str2, and if str1[i] == 'F', the substring does not equal str2. Return the lexicographically smallest string word, or empty string "" if no such string can be generated.
constraints: str2 consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Replacements to Sort the Array
description: You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums. In one operation you can replace any element of the array with any two elements that sum up to it. Return the minimum number of operations to make the array sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Count Paths That Can Form a Palindrome in a Tree
description: You are given a tree rooted at node 0 consisting of n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1 in the form of a parent array parent where parent[0] == -1, and a string s where s[i] is the character assigned to the edge between node i and parent[i]. Return the number of pairs (u, v) with u < v such that the characters on the simple path between u and v can be rearranged to form a palindrome.
constraints: s consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: The Maze III
description: There is a ball in a maze with empty spaces (0) and walls (1). The ball can go through empty spaces by rolling up, down, left, or right, but it won't stop rolling until hitting a wall or falling into a hole. Given the maze, the ball's start position, and the hole position, return the shortest instructions to drop the ball into the hole ('u', 'd', 'l', 'r'). If there are multiple shortest paths, return the lexicographically smallest one, or "impossible" if impossible.

title: Reachable Nodes In Subdivided Graph
description: You are given an undirected graph with original edges subdivided into new nodes. edges[i] = [ui, vi, cnti] indicates there are cnti new nodes on the edge between ui and vi. Given maxMoves, return the number of nodes (both original and subdivided) that are reachable from node 0 in at most maxMoves steps.

title: Find Building Where Alice and Bob Can Meet
description: You are given a 0-indexed array heights where heights[i] is the height of building i. Alice is in building a and Bob is in building b. They can move to any building j (j > a, j > b) such that heights[j] > heights[a] and heights[j] > heights[b]. Given queries where queries[i] = [ai, bi], return an array ans where ans[i] is the index of the leftmost building where Alice and Bob can meet, or -1 if impossible.

title: String Compression II
description: Run-length encoding of a string is constructed by replacing consecutive identical characters with the character followed by the count (omit count if 1). Given a string s and an integer k, return the minimum length of the run-length encoded version of s after deleting at most k characters.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.

title: Tallest Billboard
description: You have a collection of rods that can be welded together. You are given an integer array rods. You want to create two billboard supports of the exact same height using some (or none) of the rods. Return the largest possible height of your billboard installation, or 0 if impossible.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Continuous
description: You are given an integer array nums. In one operation, you can replace any element in nums with any integer. An array is continuous if all elements are unique and the difference between maximum and minimum elements equals nums.length - 1. Return the minimum number of operations to make nums continuous.

title: Human Traffic of Stadium
description: Write a solution to display the records with three or more rows with consecutive id's, and the number of people is greater than or equal to 100 for each. Return the result table ordered by visit_date in ascending order.
constraints: visit_date is the column with unique values for this table.
Each row of this table contains the visit date and visit id to the stadium with the number of people during the visit.
No two rows have the same visit_date, and day increases with id.

title: Number of Squareful Arrays
description: An array is squareful if the sum of every pair of adjacent elements is a perfect square. Given an integer array nums, return the number of permutations of nums that are squareful. Two permutations perm1 and perm2 are different if there is some index i such that perm1[i] != perm2[i].

title: Maximize the Distance Between Points on a Square
description: You are given an integer side representing the side length of a square whose bottom-left vertex is at (0, 0) and top-right at (side, side). You are given an array points of coordinates on the boundary of the square, and an integer k. Choose k points from points such that the minimum Manhattan distance between any two selected points is maximized. Return this maximum possible minimum distance.
constraints: All points lie on the perimeter of the square.

title: Stickers to Spell Word
description: We are given n different types of stickers. Each sticker has a lowercase English word on it. You would like to spell out the given string target by cutting individual letters from your collection of stickers and rearranging them. You can use each sticker more than once. Return the minimum number of stickers that you need to spell out target, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: stickers[i] and target consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Dice Roll Simulation
description: A die simulator generates a random number from 1 to 6 for each roll. You are given an integer array rollMax where rollMax[i] is the maximum number of consecutive times that the die can roll the value i + 1. Given n rolls, return the number of distinct sequences that can be obtained modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Minimum Number of Taps to Open to Water a Garden
description: There is a one-dimensional garden on the x-axis from 0 to n. There are n + 1 taps located at [0, 1, ..., n]. Given ranges where ranges[i] means tap i can water the interval [i - ranges[i], i + ranges[i]], return the minimum number of taps to open to water the entire garden [0, n], or -1 if impossible.

title: Longest Cycle in a Graph
description: You are given a directed graph of n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1, where each node has at most one outgoing edge. The graph is represented with a 0-indexed array edges of size n, indicating an edge from node i to node edges[i] (or -1 if no outgoing edge). Return the length of the longest cycle in the graph, or -1 if no cycle exists.

title: Number of ZigZag Arrays I
description: You are given three integers n, l, and r. An array of length n is called a zigzag array if its elements are in the range [l, r] and strictly alternate between increasing and decreasing (or vice versa) for every adjacent pair. Return the total number of zigzag arrays of length n modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
description: Given a string s that contains parentheses and letters, remove the minimum number of invalid parentheses to make the input string valid. Return a list of unique strings that are valid with the minimum number of removals. You may return the answer in any order.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters and parentheses '(' and ')'.
There will be at most 20 parentheses in s.

title: Maximum Number of Tasks You Can Assign
description: You have n tasks and m workers. Each task has a strength requirement tasks[i], and each worker has a strength workers[j]. A worker can complete a task if their strength is greater than or equal to the task's requirement. You also have pills magic pills that give a worker +strength extra strength. Each worker can take at most one pill. Return the maximum number of tasks that can be completed.

title: Basic Calculator IV
description: Given an expression such as expression = "e + 8 - a + 5" and an evaluation map such as {"e": 1} (given in terms of evalvars = ["e"] and evalints = [1]), return a list of tokens representing the simplified expression. An expression is simplified when terms are merged, free variables are organized in standard canonical format, and terms are sorted by degree in descending order.
constraints: expression consists of lowercase English letters, digits, '+', '-', '*', '(', ')', and ' '.
evalvars[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Moves to Move a Box to Their Target Location
description: A storekeeper is in a grid warehouse and wants to push a box to a target location. The grid consists of empty spaces ('.'), walls ('#'), player start position ('S'), box start position ('B'), and target position ('T'). The player can only push the box by walking behind it and moving in the same direction. Return the minimum number of pushes required to move the box to the target, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: There is exactly one 'B', 'S', and 'T' in the grid.

title: Remove Boxes
description: You are given several boxes with different colors represented by positive integers. You may remove several consecutive boxes of the same color k times, obtaining k * k points. Return the maximum points you can earn.

title: Painting the Walls
description: You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays, cost and time, of size n representing the costs and the time taken to paint n different walls by a paid painter. There is also a free painter that paints 1 wall in 1 unit of time for 0 cost. The free painter can only be used when the paid painter is already occupied. Return the minimum cost of painting all n walls.

title: Number of Valid Move Combinations On Chessboard
description: There is an 8 x 8 chessboard. You are given two arrays pieces and positions, where pieces[i] is the type of the ith piece ('rook', 'bishop', or 'queen') and positions[i] is its 1-indexed (row, col) coordinates. Each piece chooses a valid move direction and number of steps (or stays still) and moves simultaneously. Return the number of valid move combinations where no two pieces collide at any time during the move.

title: K Inverse Pairs Array
description: An inverse pair in an array arr is a pair of indices (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j < arr.length and arr[i] > arr[j]. Given integers n and k, return the number of different arrays consisting of numbers from 1 to n such that there are exactly k inverse pairs. Return the answer modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Count Number of Balanced Permutations
description: You are given a string num of digits. A permutation of num is called balanced if the sum of digits at even indices is equal to the sum of digits at odd indices. Return the number of distinct balanced permutations of num modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: num consists of only digits from '0' to '9'.

title: Maximum Difference Between Even and Odd Frequency II
description: You are given a string s and an integer k. Choose a substring of s of length at least k such that it contains at least two distinct characters, and find the maximum possible difference between the frequency of a character with an odd count and the frequency of a character with an even count in that substring.
constraints: s consists only of digits '0' to '4'.

title: Find the K-th Character in String Game II
description: Alice and Bob play a game. Initially, Alice has a string word = "a". You are given a 1D integer array operations. In the ith operation, Alice generates a new string by modifying word according to operations[i] (either copying word or shifting each character by 1) and appends it to word. Return the kth character of word after all operations.
constraints: The input is generated such that word will have at least k characters after all operations.

title: Design In-Memory File System
description: Design an in-memory file system to simulate the following functions: ls(path) to list directory contents or file path, mkdir(path) to create directories, addContentToFile(filePath, content) to append text to a file, and readContentFromFile(filePath) to read file contents.
constraints: path and filePath are valid absolute paths starting with '/' and separated by '/'.
At most 300 calls total will be made to ls, mkdir, addContentToFile, and readContentFromFile.

title: Count Different Palindromic Subsequences
description: Given a string s, return the number of different non-empty palindromic subsequences in s modulo 10^9 + 7. A subsequence is different if there is some index where one subsequence has a character and another does not.

title: Maximum Sum BST in Binary Tree
description: Given a binary tree root, return the maximum sum of all keys of any sub-tree which is also a Binary Search Tree (BST).
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 4 * 10^4].

title: Binary Tree Cameras
description: You are given the root of a binary tree. We install cameras on the tree nodes where each camera at a node can monitor its parent, itself, and its immediate children. Return the minimum number of cameras needed to monitor all nodes of the tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000].

title: Maximum Performance of a Team
description: You are given two integers n and k and two integer arrays speed and efficiency both of length n. There are n engineers with assigned speed and efficiency. The performance of a team is the sum of their engineers' speeds multiplied by the minimum efficiency among their engineers. Return the maximum performance of this team at most k engineers modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Trionic Array II
description: You are given an integer array nums. An array is defined as trionic if it can be partitioned into three non-empty segments such that each segment satisfies alternating parity and sum conditions. Return the maximum length of a trionic subarray.

title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equal
description: You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums and cost of length n. You can do the following operation any number of times: increase or decrease any element in nums by 1. The cost of doing one operation on the ith element is cost[i]. Return the minimum total cost to make all elements of nums equal.

title: Restore The Array
description: A program was supposed to print an array of integers. The program printed all integers concatenated as a string s, without spaces. You are also given an integer k. All original integers were in the range [1, k]. Return the number of possible arrays that could print s modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s consists of only digits and does not contain leading zeros.

title: Equal Rational Numbers
description: Given two strings s and t, each of which represents a non-negative rational number, return true if and only if they represent the same number. The strings may be in integer, finite decimal, or repeating decimal representations.
constraints: Each of s and t represents a valid rational number in the given format.
Each of s and t has length between 1 and 30.

title: Count the Number of Powerful Integers
description: You are given three integers start, finish, and limit, and a string s. An integer is called powerful if its decimal representation ends with s and each digit in the integer is at most limit. Return the count of powerful integers in the range [start, finish].
constraints: s consists of digits from '0' to '9'.
The numeric value of s as an integer is <= finish.

title: Max Stack
description: Design a max stack data structure that supports the stack operations and supports retrieving the maximum element in the stack. Implement the MaxStack class supporting push(x), pop(), top(), peekMax(), and popMax().
constraints: At most 10^4 calls will be made to push, pop, top, peekMax, and popMax.
There will be at least one element in the stack when pop, top, peekMax, or popMax is called.

title: Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs
description: You are given an integer array jobs, where jobs[i] is the amount of time it takes to complete the ith job. There are k workers you can assign jobs to. Each job should be assigned to exactly one worker. The working time of a worker is the sum of the time it takes to complete all jobs assigned to them. Return the minimum possible maximum working time of any assignment.

title: Find All Good Strings
description: Given the integers n, s1, s2, and evil. Return the number of good strings. A string is good if it has size n, it is alphabetically between s1 and s2 (inclusive), and it does not contain evil as a substring. Return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s1, s2, and evil consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Minimize the Total Price of the Trips
description: There exists an undirected and unrooted tree with n nodes indexed from 0 to n - 1. You are given the integer n and a 2D integer array edges. You are also given an array price where price[i] is the price of the ith node, and a 2D integer array trips where trips[j] = [startj, endj]. Before performing any trips, you can choose some non-adjacent nodes and halve their prices. Return the minimum total price to perform all the given trips.

title: Last Substring in Lexicographical Order
description: Given a string s, return the last substring of s in lexicographical order.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.

title: Valid Number
description: Given a string s, return true if s is a valid number. A valid number can be an integer, a decimal, or in exponential notation format optionally preceded by a sign.
constraints: s consists of only English letters (both uppercase and lowercase), digits (0-9), plus '+', minus '-', or dot '.'.

title: Edit Distance
description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2. You have three operations permitted on a word: Insert a character, Delete a character, Replace a character.
constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Range Sum Query 2D - Mutable
description: Given a 2D matrix matrix, handle multiple queries of updating the value of a cell and calculating the sum of the submatrix between indices (row1, col1) and (row2, col2). Implement the NumMatrix class.
constraints: At most 10^4 calls will be made to sumRegion and update.

title: Self Crossing
description: You are given an array of integers distance. You start at point (0,0) on an X-Y plane and you move distance[0] meters to the north, then distance[1] meters to the west, distance[2] meters to the south, distance[3] meters to the east, and so on. In other words, after each move, your direction changes counter-clockwise. Return true if your path crosses itself, and false if it does not.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
description: RandomizedCollection is a data structure that contains a collection of numbers, and allows inserting and removing specific elements and also removing a random element with equal probability across all elements. Implement the RandomizedCollection class.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^5 calls in total will be made to insert, remove, and getRandom.

title: Strong Password Checker
description: A strong password has at least 6 and at most 20 characters, at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, and one digit, and does not contain three repeating characters in a row. Given a string password, return the minimum number of steps to make password strong.
constraints: password consists of letters, digits, and special characters '!@#$%^&*()_+'.

title: Zuma Game
description: You are playing a game of Zuma. You are given a string board representing the row of balls on the board and a string hand representing the balls in your hand. When three or more consecutive balls have the same color, they will disappear. Return the minimum number of balls you have to insert to clear all the balls from the board, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: board and hand consist of the characters 'R', 'Y', 'B', 'G', and 'W'.

title: Super Washing Machines
description: You have n super washing machines on a line. Each washing machine contains some dresses. In each step, you can choose any m (1 <= m <= n) washing machines, and pass one dress from each chosen washing machine to adjacent washing machines. Given machines where machines[i] represents the number of dresses in the ith washing machine, return the minimum number of moves to make all the washing machines have the same number of dresses, or -1 if impossible.

title: Tag Validator
description: Given a string representing a code snippet, implement a tag validator to parse the code and return whether it is valid. A code snippet is valid if it is enclosed by a valid closed tag, with valid tag names, valid nested tags, and valid cdata blocks.
constraints: code consists of English letters, digits, and characters: '<', '>', '/', '!', '[', ']', ' '.

title: Non-negative Integers without Consecutive Ones
description: Given a positive integer n, return the number of the integers in the range [0, n] whose binary representations do not contain consecutive ones.

title: Course Schedule III
description: There are n different online courses numbered from 1 to n. You are given an array courses where courses[i] = [durationi, lastDayi] indicate that the ith course should be taken continuously for durationi days and must be finished before or on lastDayi. You start on day 1 and cannot take two courses concurrently. Return the maximum number of courses that you can take.

title: Cut Off Trees for Golf Event
description: You are asked to cut off all the trees in a forest for a golf event. The forest is represented as an m x n matrix where 0 represents an obstacle, 1 represents walkable flat ground, and a number greater than 1 represents a tree with that height. You must cut down the trees in order from shortest to tallest. Return the minimum steps you need to walk to cut off all the trees, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: Heights of all trees are distinct.

title: Falling Squares
description: There are several square blocks dropping on an infinite X-axis. You are given a 2D integer array positions where positions[i] = [lefti, sideLengthi] represents the ith square with side length sideLengthi dropping with its left edge aligned at lefti. After each block dropped, output the highest height of any point in the stacked blocks. Return an array of these heights.

title: Prefix and Suffix Search
description: Design a special dictionary with some words that searchs the words in it by a prefix and a suffix. Implement the WordFilter class supporting f(prefix, suffix) which returns the index of the word in the dictionary that has the given prefix and suffix. If there is more than one valid index, return the largest of them, or -1 if no such word exists.
constraints: words[i], prefix and suffix consist of lowercase English letters only.
At most 10^4 calls will be made to the function f.

title: Split Array With Same Average
description: You are given an integer array nums. You should move each element of nums into one of two arrays A and B such that A and B are non-empty, and average(A) == average(B). Return true if it is possible to achieve that and false otherwise.

title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
description: A car travels from a starting position to a destination which is target miles east of the starting position along a straight road. There are gas stations along the way. stations[i] = [positioni, fueli] represents a gas station positioni miles east of start with fueli liters of fuel. The car starts with startFuel liters of gas and uses 1 liter per mile. Return the minimum number of refueling stops to reach target, or -1 if unreachable.

title: Numbers At Most N Given Digit Set
description: Given an array of digits which is sorted in non-decreasing order. You can write numbers using each digits[i] as many times as we want. Return the number of positive integers that can be generated that are less than or equal to a given integer n.
constraints: digits[i] is a digit from '1' to '9'.
All the values in digits are unique.
digits is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Number of Music Playlists
description: Your music player contains n different songs. You want to listen to goal songs during your trip. You generate a playlist of length goal such that every song is played at least once, and a song can only be played again if at least k other songs have been played. Return the number of possible playlists modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Minimize Malware Spread
description: You are given a network of n nodes represented as an n x n adjacency matrix graph, and an array initial of initially infected nodes. When malware spreads, it infects all directly connected nodes in the same component. Suppose M(initial) is the final number of infected nodes. Remove exactly one node from initial to minimize M(initial). If multiple nodes achieve this minimum, return the node with the smallest index.
constraints: All the integers in initial are unique.

title: Three Equal Parts
description: You are given an array arr which consists of only zeros and ones, divide the array into three non-empty parts such that all of these parts represent the same binary value. If it is possible, return any [i, j] with i + 1 < j, such that arr[0..i], arr[i+1..j-1], and arr[j..arr.length-1] all represent equal binary values. If not possible, return [-1, -1].

title: Distinct Subsequences II
description: Given a string s, return the number of distinct non-empty subsequences of s. Since the answer may be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Find the Shortest Superstring
description: Given an array of strings words, return the smallest string that contains each string in words as a substring. If there are multiple valid strings of the smallest length, return any of them.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All strings in words are unique.

title: Find Servers That Handled Most Number of Requests
description: You have k servers numbered from 0 to k-1. You are given an array arrival representing arrival times of requests and load representing the time it takes to complete them. Assign requests to servers in a circular manner. Return a list of the busiest servers.

title: Find the Original Typed String II
description: You are given a string word representing the final output, and an integer k. A character may have been typed multiple times consecutively. Return the number of possible original strings of length at least k that could have resulted in word, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: word consists only of lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Cost Path with Teleportations
description: Given a grid and teleportation points, find the minimum cost to travel from the top-left to the bottom-right cell. You can teleport between designated cells.

title: Minimum Operations to Equalize Binary String
description: Given a binary string, you can perform operations to flip adjacent characters. Return the minimum operations required to make all characters equal.

title: Maximum XOR Score Subarray Queries
description: You are given an array nums and a list of queries. For each query, return the maximum XOR score of any subarray within the queried range.

title: Count Special Integers
description: We call a positive integer special if all of its digits are distinct. Given a positive integer n, return the number of special integers that belong to the interval [1, n].

title: Closest Subsequence Sum
description: You are given an integer array nums and an integer goal. You want to choose a subsequence of nums such that the sum of its elements is the closest possible to goal. Return the minimum absolute difference.

title: Consecutive Numbers Sum
description: Given an integer n, return the number of ways you can write n as the sum of consecutive positive integers.

title: Sum of Perfect Square Ancestors
description: Given a tree, calculate the sum of ancestor values that are perfect squares for each node.

title: Stone Game V
description: Alice and Bob play a game with an array of stones. Alice divides the row into two non-empty parts, and Bob throws away the part with the maximum sum. Alice's score increases by the sum of the remaining part. Return the maximum score Alice can obtain.

title: Create Sorted Array through Instructions
description: Given an integer array instructions, you are asked to create a sorted array from the elements in instructions. The cost of inserting an element is the minimum of elements strictly less than it and strictly greater than it. Return the total cost modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time
description: Given a graph of cities, passing fees, and edges with travel times, return the minimum cost to travel from city 0 to city n-1 within maxTime minutes.

title: Minimum Swaps To Make Sequences Increasing
description: You are given two integer arrays of the same length nums1 and nums2. In one operation, you are allowed to swap nums1[i] with nums2[i]. Return the minimum number of needed operations to make nums1 and nums2 strictly increasing.

title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal to Target
description: You are given two positive integer arrays nums and target, of the same length. In a single operation, you can select any subarray of nums and increment or decrement each element by 1. Return the minimum number of operations required to make nums equal to target.

title: Find the K-Sum of an Array
description: You are given an integer array nums and a positive integer k. You can choose any subsequence of the array and sum all of its elements. Return the kth largest sum among all possible subsequences.

title: Maximum Total Subarray Value II
description: Given an integer array nums, you need to find the maximum possible total value of non-overlapping subarrays that meet specific criteria.

title: Count Palindromic Subsequences
description: Given a string of digits s, return the number of palindromic subsequences of s having length 5. Since the answer may be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Block Placement Queries
description: You are given an empty boolean array and queries to either place a block at a given position or query if a block of a certain size can be placed before a given position. Return a boolean array for the queries.
